cards.t: Health risks of prolonged ICT use
cards.tz: 长时间使用 ICT 的健康风险
cards.en:
Prolonged use of computers and mobile devices without a proper posture and workstation set-up increases several health risks. The book lists five you must name in exams:
  • Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI): pain or numbness in fingers and wrists caused by repetitive movements such as clicking a mouse or pressing keys.
  • Eyestrain: tired eyes or blurred vision from staring at a monitor too long or bad lighting.
  • Back and neck problems: caused by poor posture or sitting immobile for too long (e.g. "tech neck" from looking down at a phone).
  • Deep vein thrombosis (DVT): blood clots in the legs from prolonged sitting; it can be fatal if the clot travels to the lungs.
  • Tired legs (leg fatigue) when feet are not supported.
In an answer, always pair a health risk with its cause, then give a matching ergonomic product or habit.
cards.zh:
如果长时间用电脑/手机而姿势和工作台设置不当，会增加以下健康风险（考试要会写出名称和成因）：
  • Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) 重复性劳损：手指、手腕疼痛或麻木，因为重复动作（点鼠标、按键盘）。
  • Eyestrain 眼睛疲劳：盯屏幕太久或光线不好，眼睛累、视线模糊。
  • Back and neck problem 腰背及颈部问题：姿势差或久坐不动，例如低头看手机造成的 "tech neck"。
  • Deep vein thrombosis 深静脉血栓：久坐令腿部形成血块，血块流到肺部可致命。
  • Tired legs 腿部疲劳：脚没有承托。
答题时要写：健康问题 + 成因 + 对应的人体工学产品或习惯。

ex.q: Ada programs for 8 hours continuously every day. Name a possible health risk and suggest an ergonomic product to solve it.
ex.a:
Health risk: Repetitive Strain Injury (RSI) in the wrist/fingers caused by repetitive typing and mouse clicking.
Product: a mouse pad with wrist rest (or an ergonomic keyboard/mouse) which keeps the wrist straight and natural.
ex.az: 健康风险：RSI（重复打字、点鼠标）。产品：带护腕的鼠标垫/人体工学键盘，让手腕保持平直。

cards.t: Correct sitting posture and workstation set-up
cards.tz: 正确坐姿与工作台设置
cards.en:
Fig. 2.3 of the book shows the correct computer workstation:
  • Ergonomic monitor: height and angle adjustable; the viewing angle is slightly downward (about 30°) so you do not bend the neck.
  • Armrest: height adjustable; keep the forearm horizontal and relaxed.
  • Mouse pad with wrist rest: keeps the wrist straight, reducing RSI.
  • Ergonomic chair: back rest and height adjustable; knees at about 90°.
  • Footrest: keeps the feet flat and reduces posture problems / leg fatigue.
  • Window blinds: block strong sunlight and reduce light reflections (glare) on the screen.
Without a footrest, you can lower the chair or the table/monitor so the feet rest flat.
cards.zh:
课本 Fig. 2.3 的正确工作台：
  • Ergonomic monitor：可调高度和角度，视线稍微向下（约30°），不用弯颈。
  • Armrest 扶手：可调高度，前臂保持水平放松。
  • Mouse pad with wrist rest：手腕保持平直，减少 RSI。
  • Ergonomic chair：椅背和高度可调，膝盖约 90°。
  • Footrest 脚踏：双脚平放，减少腿部疲劳和姿势问题。
  • Window blinds 百叶帘：挡强光、减少屏幕反光。
没有脚踏时，可调低椅子，并相应调整桌子/显示器高度，让脚平放地上。

ex.q: Peter's feet hang above the floor when he sits at the computer. (a) Which product prevents leg fatigue? (b) Without it, what should he adjust?
ex.a:
(a) A footrest.
(b) Lower the height of the chair so his feet are flat, and then adjust the height of the table and monitor (and its viewing angle) to keep a correct posture. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.1 Q5 answer: D, all four.)
ex.az: (a) 脚踏。(b) 调低椅子，再调整桌子、显示器高度和角度保持正确姿势。

cards.tz: 手机与平板的正确姿势
cards.en:
Mobile devices create their own posture problems. Looking down at a phone bends the neck forward, giving "tech neck" (neck and shoulder pain). Constant typing on small touch screens can cause text claw (finger/wrist pain, a type of RSI).
Correct practice (Fig. 2.4):
  • Smartphone: keep the phone at eye level instead of bending the head down.
  • Tablet: lift up the tablet by a pillow or stand so you are not looking down at your lap.
  • For long typing on a tablet, use a tablet stand + external (wireless) keyboard: the stand raises the screen to eye level (protects neck) and the keyboard lets the wrists stay natural.
  • Use a rest reminder app that pushes a rest notification; it should not force-close apps or turn off the device.
cards.zh:
手机平板也有姿势问题：低头看手机令颈部前倾，造成 "tech neck" 低头族颈痛；长时间在小屏幕打字会造成 text claw（手指手腕痛，属 RSI）。
正确做法：
  • 手机：把手机举到视线高度，不要低头。
  • 平板：用枕头或支架垫高。
  • 长时间打字：平板支架 + 外接（无线）键盘，支架令屏幕到视线高度保护颈部，键盘令手腕自然。
  • 安装休息提醒 app，推送休息通知即可（不是强制关 app 或关机）。

ex.q: George types essays on a tablet using a stand and a wireless keyboard. How are these related to ergonomic design?
ex.a:
The tablet stand raises the screen to a suitable height/viewing angle so George need not bend his neck, reducing neck and back pain.
The separate keyboard can be placed so that his forearms are horizontal and wrists stay straight, and physical keys are easier to type on than the touch screen, reducing RSI.
ex.az: 支架：屏幕升到合适高度，减少颈背痛。键盘：手腕平直，减少 RSI。

cards.tz: 人体工学的定义与目的
cards.en:
Ergonomics is a science-based discipline about designing or arranging workplaces, products and systems to suit the people who use them.
Its aim is to optimise the strengths and abilities of people and minimise the risk of injury or harm by improving the tools and environments for working, resting and playing.
Key idea: the design fits the user, not the user forcing himself to fit the design. That is why so many items are adjustable (chair height, armrest, monitor angle): different users have different body sizes.
Example: gaming chairs sell well (sales up over 50% in 2020) because of comfortable material and ergonomic design: adjustable seat, backrest and armrests support people who sit for hours. In-ear headphones, mice and keyboards are also ergonomic products.
cards.zh:
Ergonomics（人体工学）是一门以科学为基础的学科，研究如何设计或安排工作场所、产品和系统，使其适合使用者。
目的：发挥人的长处和能力，减少受伤或伤害的风险，方法是改善工作、休息和娱乐时的工具和环境。
核心：设计去配合用户，而不是用户迁就设计，所以很多东西都可调节（椅高、扶手、显示器角度），适合不同身形。
例子：电竞椅 2020 年销量升逾 50%，卖点是舒适物料和人体工学设计（可调座椅、椅背、扶手）。入耳式耳机、鼠标、键盘也是人体工学产品。

ex.q: Explain why an office buys chairs with adjustable height instead of fixed chairs.
ex.a: Ergonomics designs products to suit the people who use them. Staff have different body sizes, so an adjustable chair lets each user keep the feet flat and knees at about 90°, reducing back pain, leg fatigue and the risk of injury.
ex.az: 员工身形不同，可调椅能适合每个人，减少腰背痛和腿部疲劳。

cards.tz: 电脑用的人体工学产品
cards.en:
Table 2.1 lists six ergonomic designs and the problem each solves:
ProductBenefit
Ergonomic mouse (vertical)hand held in a natural handshake position, avoids twisting the wrist, reduces RSI
Ergonomic mouse pad (wrist rest)keeps wrist straight, reduces RSI
Ergonomic keyboard (split/curved)natural hand and wrist angle, reduces RSI
Adjustable laptop standraises the screen to eye level, reduces neck pain
Ergonomic chairadjustable height, back rest, armrest, neck rest: reduces back/neck pain
Dual monitorsless time switching tabs; place both at arm's length and use a swivel chair to avoid neck twisting
Summary table: RSI → wrist-rest pad, ergonomic mouse, chair armrest; Eyestrain → window blinds, sufficient lighting; Tired legs → footrest; Back/neck pain → chair with neck and back rest, height/angle adjustable monitor.
cards.zh:
Table 2.1 六种人体工学设计：
  • 人体工学鼠标（直立式）：手像握手姿势，避免手腕扭转，减少 RSI。
  • 护腕鼠标垫：手腕平直。
  • 人体工学键盘（分体/弧形）：手腕角度自然。
  • 可调笔记本支架：屏幕升到视线高度，减颈痛。
  • 人体工学椅：可调高度、椅背、扶手、头枕。
  • 双显示器：少切换分页提升效率；两屏放在一臂距离，用转椅避免扭颈（不是上下叠放）。
总结：RSI→护腕垫、人体工学鼠标、扶手；眼疲劳→百叶帘、足够照明；腿累→脚踏；颈背痛→带头枕椅背的椅子、可调显示器。

ex.q: Peter will use dual monitors. Which set-up is ergonomic: (1) swivel chair to avoid neck twisting (2) both monitors at arm's length (3) one monitor above the other?
ex.a: (1) and (2) only. A swivel chair lets him turn his body instead of twisting the neck, and both screens at arm's length avoid eyestrain. Stacking monitors forces him to tilt the head up, causing neck strain.
ex.az: (1)(2)。叠放要抬头，会伤颈。

cards.t: Taking breaks: the 20-20-20 rule and stretching
cards.tz: 休息习惯：20-20-20 法则与伸展
cards.en:
Apart from posture and furniture, taking regular breaks and exercising are key to minimising injury. Since a new routine is hard to build, use break reminder software (e.g. EyeRest) to remind you.
  • 20-20-20 rule (prevents eyestrain): every 20 minutes, look at something 20 feet (6 m) away for 20 seconds. This lets the eyes relax and refocus.
  • Prevent muscle strain: sitting in the same position for long periods causes aches; take a 5-minute break to stretch and move every hour.
Moving regularly also lowers the risk of deep vein thrombosis.
cards.zh:
除了姿势和家具，定时休息和运动是减少伤害的关键。新习惯难建立，可用休息提醒软件（如 EyeRest）。
  • 20-20-20 法则（防眼疲劳）：每 20 分钟，看 20 英尺（6 米）外的东西 20 秒，让眼睛放松、重新对焦。
  • 防肌肉劳损：久坐同一姿势会酸痛，每小时休息 5 分钟伸展走动。
多走动也减低深静脉血栓风险。

ex.q: A student studies on a computer from 2:00 pm to 4:00 pm. Using the book's rules, how many 20-second eye breaks and how many 5-minute stretch breaks should he take?
ex.a:
Eye breaks every 20 minutes: 120 ÷ 20 = 6 (at 2:20, 2:40, …, 4:00; about 5 during the session plus one at the end).
Stretch breaks every hour: 120 ÷ 60 = 2 (at 3:00 and 4:00).
ex.az: 眼睛休息约 6 次（每 20 分钟），伸展 2 次（每小时）。

cards.en:
Ergonomics is not only about physical aspects (body size, dominant hand) but also the user's age, strength, technological experience, skill/knowledge, cultural expectation and goals. Ergonomic and user-friendly features are important in software design. A lack of ergonomic design frustrates users (Fig. 2.9).
Examples of user-friendly interface features: a zoom command for users with poor eyesight; consistent terms throughout the app; grouping options (e.g. stations grouped by rail line instead of a full list); sufficient colour contrast between text and background; adjustable font size; clear navigation and help texts.
Note: a log-in password is a security feature, not an ergonomic one.
cards.zh:
人体工学不只是身体尺寸、惯用手，也要考虑用户的年龄、力气、科技经验、技能知识、文化期望和目标。软件设计中，人体工学和用户友好功能很重要，缺乏会令用户沮丧。
例子：为视力差者提供缩放 zoom；全程用词一致；把选项分组（按铁路线分车站而不是一长串）；文字与背景颜色对比足够；可调字体大小；清晰导航和说明。
注意：登录密码是保安功能，不是人体工学设计。

ex.q: Which are ergonomic interface features? (1) zoom for poor eyesight (2) consistent terms (3) stations grouped by rail line (4) sufficient colour contrast
ex.a: All of (1), (2), (3) and (4). Each one reduces the user's effort or suits users' abilities (eyesight, memory, efficiency).
ex.az: 全部都是。

cards.tz: 界面设计准则：一致、效率、记忆
cards.en:
The book's ergonomics guidelines for interface design:
  • Consistency: saves time on adapting to the application design. Keep terminologies, action sequences and graphics consistent (e.g. all icons in the same style).
  • Efficiency: suitable features for both unexperienced and advanced users; break complex tasks into simpler tasks; less is more, avoid distraction (clean layout); acceptable waiting time.
  • Memory: minimise users' memory load, using generic actions, universal signages (icons people already know), and clear navigations and help texts. Example: a date-of-birth input split into Year / Month / Day fields with placeholders and specific error messages ("Select your birth month") is better than one box "2033/14/12" with just "Error".
Web page UI is discussed further in Core C section 4.4.
cards.zh:
课本的界面设计人体工学准则：
  • Consistency 一致性：减少适应时间；术语、操作次序、图像保持一致。
  • Efficiency 效率：同时照顾新手和熟手；把复杂任务拆成简单步骤；少即是多，避免干扰；可接受的等待时间。
  • Memory 记忆：减少用户记忆负担：通用操作、通用标志、清晰导航和说明。例：出生日期分成年/月/日三格并有具体错误提示，比一个格子只显示 "Error" 好。

ex.q: A form asks for date of birth in one text box and shows only "Error" when the format is wrong. Suggest TWO improvements based on ergonomic guidelines.
ex.a:
1. Split into separate Year / Month / Day fields (or drop-down lists) with placeholders such as YYYY, MM, so users need not remember the format (minimise memory load).
2. Show clear, specific help/error texts, e.g. "Enter a valid year" / "Select your birth month", so users know how to fix it.
ex.az: 分开年月日栏（下拉）；给出清晰具体的错误提示。

cards.t: Misconception: ergonomics is only about furniture
cards.tz: 误解：人体工学只关于家具
cards.en:
Wrong: "Ergonomics only means comfortable chairs and desks."
Correct: ergonomics covers physical products (chair, mouse, keyboard, stand, footrest, blinds), work habits (breaks, 20-20-20 rule, stretching) and software/user interface design (consistency, efficiency, memory load, colour contrast, font size). The Chapter Summary stresses: "Ergonomics is not only related to the furniture and workstation set-up. Ergonomic and user-friendly features are important in software design."
Another trap: security features (password, anti-virus) improve safety of data, not the comfort or efficiency of the user, so they are not ergonomic designs. Also, products must match the problem: a footrest does not prevent RSI in the wrist; a wrist rest does.
cards.zh:
错误：“人体工学只是舒服的桌椅。”
正确：包括实体产品（椅、鼠标、键盘、支架、脚踏、百叶帘）、使用习惯（休息、20-20-20、伸展）以及软件/界面设计（一致性、效率、记忆负担、颜色对比、字体大小）。
另一陷阱：保安功能（密码、防毒）不是人体工学设计。产品要对症：脚踏不能防手腕 RSI，护腕才可以；显示器角度、灯光也与 RSI 无关。

ex.q: Which practice prevents RSI in fingers and wrists from clicking a mouse? A footrest / angle-adjustable monitor / good lighting / wrist rest
ex.a: Use a wrist rest to keep the wrist natural. The others address leg fatigue, neck pain and eyestrain respectively.
ex.az: 护腕。其余分别对应腿累、颈痛、眼疲劳。

cards.tz: 网络成瘾的征兆和症状
cards.en:
Surfing the Internet for 1-2 hours after finishing important tasks may just be a habit. But if you are unable to stop yourself from surfing for prolonged periods, and even end up late for or missing important tasks, it is very likely an addiction.
Signs and symptoms in the book:
  • Prioritising Internet use over necessary life tasks
  • Thinking about the Internet even when you are offline (e.g. during lessons)
  • Being moody and irritable when Internet access is restricted
Examples of Internet addiction: online game addiction, social media addiction, compulsive video streaming, gadget addiction. Watching one movie every night by itself is not a symptom: it is a planned leisure habit.
cards.zh:
完成重要事情后上网 1-2 小时可能只是习惯；但如果无法停止长时间上网，甚至因此迟到或错过重要事情，就很可能是成瘾。
症状：
  • 上网优先于必要的生活事务
  • 离线时也在想网络（如上课时）
  • 限制上网时情绪化、易怒
类型：网络游戏成瘾、社交媒体成瘾、沉迷串流影片、电子产品成瘾。每晚看一套电影本身不算症状。

ex.q: Which are symptoms of Internet addiction? (1) watching a movie on a streaming site every night (2) upset when cannot connect (3) thinking about the Internet during lessons (4) prioritising Internet over important tasks
ex.a: (2), (3) and (4) only. (1) alone is a normal habit if it does not interfere with important tasks. (Textbook Ch2 Exercise MC7: C)

cards.en:
Apart from physical health hazards, Internet addiction also harms mental health, leading to poor social relationships and a decrease in quality of life (Fig. 2.10).
Physical healthMental health
Fatigue
Muscle strain
Poor sleep
Unintentional weight loss/gain		Poor memory
Anxiety and depression
Concentration difficulty
Extreme case (Activity 2.2): a 17-year-old game addict played online games for 40 hours continuously, argued with his family and committed suicide. Social impact: arguments with family, isolation, phubbing. Diseases like diabetes are not listed as a direct result.
cards.zh:
除了身体健康，网络成瘾也损害心理健康，导致人际关系变差、生活质量下降。
身体心理
疲劳
肌肉劳损
睡眠差
体重意外下降/上升		记忆力差
焦虑和抑郁
难以集中
极端例子：17 岁少年连续玩网游 40 小时，与家人争执后自杀。社交影响：与家人冲突、孤立、phubbing。糖尿病不属课本所列的直接影响。

ex.q: George reads social media posts for 6 hours every day. Which will NOT arise directly from his Internet addiction: poor sleep, blurry vision, anxiety, diabetes?
ex.a: Diabetes. Poor sleep and anxiety are listed impacts, and blurry vision comes from eyestrain. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.2 Q1: D)
ex.az: 糖尿病。

cards.en:
Ways to prevent Internet addiction (from the book's discussion and checkpoints):
  • Set time limits and finish important tasks first; use screen-time / rest reminder apps.
  • Have a hobby other than Internet surfing (sport, music, reading).
  • Spend time face to face with family and friends; avoid phubbing.
  • Parents/schools: talk openly, education on healthy use.
Game design to prevent teen addiction (Checkpoint 2.2 Q2): playtime limit / anti-addiction system that forces logout after a set time; break reminders after continuous play; real-name / age verification to apply limits to minors; no rewards for continuous log-in (reduce "daily streak" pressure); spending limits on in-game purchases.
cards.zh:
预防网络成瘾：
  • 设定时间限制，先完成重要事情；用屏幕时间/休息提醒 app。
  • 培养上网以外的兴趣（运动、音乐、阅读）。
  • 多与家人朋友面对面相处，不要 phubbing。
  • 家长、学校沟通和教育。
游戏中的防沉迷设计：游戏时间上限（到时强制登出）；连续玩一段时间后休息提醒；实名/年龄验证；取消连续登录奖励；消费上限。

ex.q: Patrick is a game developer. Suggest TWO designs to prevent teens from game addiction and describe them.
ex.a:
1. Daily playtime limit: after e.g. 2 hours in a day, a minor account is logged out automatically.
2. Rest reminder: after 1 hour of continuous play, a pop-up asks the player to take a break, and rewards stop until a break is taken.
(Also accept: age verification, removing log-in streak rewards, spending limits.)
ex.az: 每日游戏时间上限；连续玩一小时提示休息。

cards.en:
Phubbing (phone snubbing) is a new word describing the act of ignoring someone you are with in person and paying attention to your mobile device instead.
Research has shown that phubbing affects relationships by making ignored people feel they are excluded or less important. It is one way Internet/smartphone addiction harms social relationships.
Example: friends at dinner each looking at their own phone, hardly talking. Prevention: put the phone away during meals, turn off notifications, agree on "no phone" times with family.
cards.zh:
Phubbing（phone snubbing）：和别人面对面时不理对方，只顾看手机。
研究显示 phubbing 会令被忽视的人觉得被排斥或不重要，影响关系，是手机/网络成瘾损害人际关系的一种表现。
例：朋友聚餐各自看手机。预防：吃饭时收起手机、关通知、和家人约定无手机时间。

ex.q: Explain how phubbing affects relationships, with an example.
ex.a: Phubbing means ignoring the person you are with to look at your phone. E.g. a son keeps scrolling social media during family dinner; his parents feel excluded and less important, communication drops and the relationship becomes distant.
ex.az: 例：晚饭时只顾看手机，父母觉得被冷落，沟通减少。

cards.en:
The development of the Internet brings freedom of information: we are free to express ourselves online and access information distributed by others.
The Internet has changed everyday life (Fig. 2.11):
  • Daily service: e-books at public libraries, news, social media, education.
  • E-commerce: mobile payment, food delivery, ride-hailing, consumer goods.
  • Small office/Home office (SOHO): video conferencing, remote working, cloud collaboration.
However, freedom does not justify the acts of harming others and society, e.g. spreading fake news, cyberbullying, scamming, social engineering and copyright infringement. Abusing freedom of information leads to serious legal consequences, including fines and imprisonment.
cards.zh:
互联网带来资讯自由：我们可以在网上自由表达，并取得别人发布的资讯。
互联网改变了生活：
  • 日常服务：公共图书馆电子书、新闻、社交媒体、教育。
  • 电子商贸：流动支付、外卖、网约车、消费品。
  • SOHO 小型/家居办公室：视像会议、遥距工作、云端协作。
但自由不代表可以伤害他人和社会，如散播假新闻、网络欺凌、诈骗、社交工程、侵犯版权。滥用资讯自由会带来罚款和监禁等严重法律后果。

ex.q: Give one example each of how the Internet changed daily service, e-commerce and SOHO.
ex.a:
Daily service: borrowing e-books from the public library online.
E-commerce: ordering food delivery and paying by mobile payment.
SOHO: working remotely with video conferencing and cloud collaboration.
ex.az: 电子书；外卖+流动支付；遥距工作+视像会议。

cards.t: Pros and cons of freedom of information (Table 2.2)
cards.tz: 资讯自由的优点与缺点
cards.en:
ProsCons
Up-to-date informationOut-of-date information
A wide variety of informationLack of quality control
Huge amount of informationOffensive content
Mostly free of chargeFake information
Accessible anytime and anywhereCopyright infringement
Easy exchange of informationInternet addiction
Personal data breach
Why "up-to-date" and "out-of-date" both appear: news is posted instantly, but old pages stay online and are not removed or updated. "Lack of quality control": anyone can publish without editing or checking, so accuracy is not guaranteed.
cards.zh:
优点缺点
资讯最新资讯过时
种类多缺乏质量控制
数量大冒犯性内容
大多免费虚假资讯
随时随地取得侵犯版权
交流容易网络成瘾
个人资料外泄
为何“最新”和“过时”同时出现：新消息即时发布，但旧网页一直留在网上没有更新。“缺乏质量控制”：任何人都可发布，没有编辑审核。

ex.q: A student says: "Information on the Internet is always up to date and reliable." Evaluate this statement using the pros and cons of freedom of information.
ex.a: Partly true: news is posted instantly so information can be up-to-date. But old pages remain online, so some information is out-of-date; and since anyone can publish, there is lack of quality control and fake information. So information must be fact-checked before use.
ex.az: 部分正确：可以很新，但也有过时、缺乏审核和假资讯，要查证。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌的定义与形式
cards.en:
A survey shows that nearly half of the students in Hong Kong have experienced cyberbullying.
Cyberbullying is a kind of bullying and harassment that occurs over the Internet. It can occur on messaging apps, social media, games, forums or any other platform where people can view and interact with each other.
Forms shown in the book: in-game abuse ("Loser!", "Bad gamer!", "Your fault!"), insulting comments on someone's photo in a class group chat (Fig. 2.13), abusive messages such as "When will you die?", reposting someone's photos with teasing comments, doxxing, and spreading rumours.
Real cases: a Japanese Netflix star committed suicide after months of online abuse (a man was fined); K-pop stars Sulli and Goo Hara died by suicide in 2019. These sparked calls for new laws.
cards.zh:
调查显示近一半香港学生曾遭网络欺凌。
网络欺凌是透过互联网进行的欺凌和骚扰。可发生在即时通讯 app、社交媒体、游戏、论坛等任何可互相浏览和互动的平台。
形式：游戏内辱骂（"Loser!"）、在班群嘲笑某人照片、发 "When will you die?" 这类恶毒讯息、转贴别人照片并嘲笑、起底、散播谣言。
真实个案：日本 Netflix 明星被网络辱骂数月后自杀（有人被罚款）；韩星雪莉、具荷拉 2019 年自杀。引发立法呼声。

ex.q: In a class group chat, A posts B's photo and others write "So ugly" and "I'm having dinner, so disgusting!". Explain why this is cyberbullying.
ex.a: It is harassment over the Internet (an instant messenger group): the messages are insulting and repeated by several people, can be viewed by the whole class, and are meant to hurt B. Joking does not make people feel bad, but bullying does.
ex.az: 这是在网上（班群）的骚扰和侮辱，多人参与，全班可见，目的是伤害 B。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌对心理健康的风险
cards.en:
Joking does not make people feel bad but bullying does. Victims of cyberbullying feel lonely, sad, angry and frightened. They may become insecure and isolate themselves from others.
Common emotional consequences: depression and eating disorders. In extreme cases, cyberbullying may even lead to self-harm and suicide.
Why online bullying can be worse than offline: it can happen 24/7, content spreads to a large audience fast, it stays online (hard to delete), and bullies can be anonymous.
cards.zh:
开玩笑不会令人难受，欺凌会。受害者感到孤独、伤心、愤怒、害怕，可能变得缺乏安全感并自我孤立。
常见情绪后果：抑郁、饮食失调；极端情况自残、自杀。
为何比现实欺凌更严重：全天候发生；内容迅速传给大量人；留在网上难以删除；欺凌者可匿名。

ex.q: John's photos are reposted on a forum and users leave offensive comments. State one common emotional impact on John.
ex.a: John may feel sad / frightened / lonely, become insecure and isolate himself; it may lead to depression. (Any one, 1 mark.)
ex.az: 伤心、害怕、孤独、抑郁（任一）。

cards.en:
Prevention: avoid sharing sensitive personal information online with people you do not know, because bullies often hurt targets with information available online (e.g. set the account to private, only close friends can see). Set a good example by not participating in cyberbullying (don't forward, like or comment).
WhoActions
VictimsTell someone you trust; do not respond, you can also block the bullies; collect the evidence (screenshots) and report to the authorities or service providers
Support the victimsListen to and stay with the victim; advise the victim to follow the above suggestions
Policy and educationImplement anti-cyberbullying policies and laws, such as the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance and Defamation Ordinance; promote anti-cyberbullying to students and the public
cards.zh:
预防：不要向陌生人分享敏感个人资料，欺凌者常利用网上资料伤人（帐户设为私人，只给好友看）；以身作则，不参与欺凌（不转发、不点赞、不留言）。
对象做法
受害者告诉信任的人；不回应，可封锁欺凌者；保留证据（截图）并向当局或服务供应商举报
支持受害者聆听、陪伴；建议他按上述去做
政策和教育反欺凌政策和法例，例如《个人资料(私隐)条例》、《诽谤条例》；向学生和公众推广

ex.q: Ms Wong is John's teacher and wants to help him after his photos were reposted with offensive comments. Suggest TWO actions she can do.
ex.a:
1. Listen to and stay with John to support him emotionally.
2. Advise him to collect evidence (screenshots) and report to the forum administrator / police, and to block the users.
(Also: inform parents/school social worker; promote anti-cyberbullying in class.)
ex.az: 聆听陪伴；建议截图存证并向论坛/警方举报。

cards.en:
"Doxxing" (起底) refers to the act of gathering and revealing others' private personal information on the Internet, such as on social media platforms and forums (e.g. posting someone's phone number, address, school, photos).
Doxxing is unethical and can lead to serious legal consequences including fines and imprisonment. In Hong Kong it falls under the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance: disclosing someone's personal data without consent with intent to gain benefit or cause loss.
Doxxing is often a tool of cyberbullying because it lets others harass the target offline as well.
cards.zh:
Doxxing（起底）指在网上搜集并公开他人的私人个人资料（如在社交媒体、论坛贴出电话、地址、学校、照片）。
起底不道德，可导致罚款和监禁。在香港属《个人资料(私隐)条例》范围：未经同意披露他人个人资料，意图获利或令其受损。
起底常被用作网络欺凌工具，令目标在现实中也受滋扰。

ex.q: George posts Amy's phone number and photos on social media because he dislikes her. Which law may he break?
ex.a: The Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance: he disclosed Amy's personal data without consent, intending to cause harm (doxxing). Penalty: fines and imprisonment.
ex.az: 《个人资料(私隐)条例》，起底。

cards.tz: 网络欺凌：旁观者应如何做
cards.en:
Misconception: "I only forwarded the message; I'm not the bully." Forwarding, liking or joining an online attack spreads the harm and makes you part of the cyberbullying. It may also break the law (e.g. reposting defamatory content).
Misconception: "The victim should reply and argue back." The book advises victims not to respond; replying usually escalates the attack. Instead block, keep evidence and report.
Example (Chapter Exercise LQ3): Paul posts "Peter stole my phone! Let's beat him after school!" Jennie should not forward it or join because the accusation may be false (defamation), and it incites violence. She should report it to a teacher and/or tell Peter.
cards.zh:
误解：“我只是转发，不是欺凌者。”转发、点赞、加入围攻都会扩散伤害，令你成为欺凌的一份子，甚至可能违法（转贴诽谤内容）。
误解：“受害者应该回骂。”课本建议不要回应，回应通常令攻击升级；应封锁、保留证据、举报。
例：Paul 在班群说“Peter 偷了我的手机！放学打他！”Jennie 不应转发或参与：指控可能是假的（诽谤），且煽动暴力。应告诉老师。

ex.q: Jennie receives "Peter stole my phone! Let's beat him after school!" (a) Suggest TWO reasons she does not forward it or join. (b) What action should she take?
ex.a:
(a) The claim may be false/unverified and forwarding it may harm Peter's reputation (Defamation); beating someone is violence/illegal and joining makes her part of the bullying.
(b) Report the message to a teacher/school (keep a screenshot as evidence).
ex.az: (a) 未经证实可能是诽谤；打人违法、参与即欺凌。(b) 截图报告老师。

cards.tz: 资讯可靠性与事实查证
cards.en:
In an era of information explosion, it is important to stop the spread of misinformation by evaluating the reliability of information, i.e. fact-checking.
When you read information, examine its reliability, validity, accuracy, authority, timeliness and bias by comparing various sources. Do not share or comment when you are not sure if the information is true or not.
Slogan (Fig. 2.17): Stop, Think and Check before spreading information.
Example of fake news: a post claiming typhoon signal No. 10 times "from the Hong Kong Observatory" by a random account (ABC_123), shared 256 times. Check with the official source (Observatory website) first. (Information evaluation in detail: Core C section 3.3.)
cards.zh:
在资讯爆炸年代，要通过评估资讯的可靠性，即事实查证，阻止错误资讯散播。
阅读资讯时，通过比较不同来源，检查其可靠性、有效性、准确性、权威性、时效性和偏见。不确定真假时，不要分享或留言。
口号：Stop, Think and Check（停、想、查）。
例：某帐号 ABC_123 声称收到天文台通知的台风讯号时间表，被分享 256 次；应先到官方来源（天文台网站）核实。

ex.q: A forum article claims an idol was a school bully. Patrick reposts it and leaves offensive comments; later it is proved fake. What should Patrick have done?
ex.a: He should have fact-checked the claim by comparing with other reliable sources (e.g. official statements, reputable news) and not shared or commented while unsure. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.3 Q1: A)
ex.az: 先与其他来源核实，不确定就不分享不留言。

cards.en:
Six criteria named in the book, with questions to ask:
  • Reliability: is the source trustworthy (official, reputable)?
  • Validity: is the information logical and supported by evidence?
  • Accuracy: are facts, numbers and quotes correct? Do other sources agree?
  • Authority: who is the author/organisation? Are they an expert?
  • Timeliness: when was it published or updated? Is it out of date?
  • Bias: is it one-sided, an advertisement, or trying to make you angry?
Method: compare various sources. Red flags: anonymous account, no date, emotional headline, "forward to everyone", too good to be true (e.g. a $500 coupon bug).
cards.zh:
课本六个准则：
  • Reliability 可靠性：来源是否可信（官方、有信誉）？
  • Validity 有效性：是否合理、有证据？
  • Accuracy 准确性：事实数字是否正确？其他来源是否一致？
  • Authority 权威性：作者/机构是谁，是否专家？
  • Timeliness 时效性：何时发布/更新，会否过时？
  • Bias 偏见：是否片面、广告、煽动情绪？
方法：比较多个来源。警号：匿名帐号、无日期、煽情标题、“请转发”、好得难以置信。

ex.q: A WhatsApp message says "Factories in mainland China have stopped making toilet paper! Buy now!" Use THREE criteria to evaluate it.
ex.a:
Authority/Reliability: no named source or official body, forwarded many times, so unreliable.
Accuracy: compare with government announcements and reputable news, which say supply is normal.
Bias: emotional wording urging panic buying.
Conclusion: do not forward; it caused 2020 panic buying.
ex.az: 无来源、与官方消息不符、煽动情绪，不应转发。

cards.en:
The impact of trusting or spreading wrong information grows with its scale:
  • Wrong information in a school assignment → affects your score.
  • False weather information → affects your plan.
  • Reposting fake news that harms someone's image → hurts their feelings, damages reputation.
  • Misinformation that causes social chaos → may even endanger national security.
Everyone has the responsibility to think critically before spreading any information.
Case: in 2020, false rumours on supply shortage spread over instant messages and social media (production in mainland stopped; imports affected by border restrictions) and triggered toilet paper and dry grocery panic buying in Hong Kong. The government also takes measures to stop misinformation.
cards.zh:
错误资讯的影响随规模变大：
  • 功课用错资料→影响分数。
  • 错误天气资讯→影响计划。
  • 转发损害别人形象的假新闻→伤害对方。
  • 引起社会混乱→甚至危害国家安全。
每个人都有责任在散播资讯前批判思考。
个案：2020 年供应短缺谣言经即时通讯和社交媒体流传，引发香港厕纸和干货抢购潮。

ex.q: Explain how a false rumour can lead to panic buying.
ex.a: The rumour (e.g. supply will stop) spreads quickly through instant messages and social media; many people believe it without fact-checking and rush to buy, shelves become empty, which seems to 'confirm' the rumour and makes more people panic. Real shortage and social chaos follow.
ex.az: 谣言快速传播→大家不查证就抢购→货架清空→更多人恐慌。

cards.tz: 法律后果：《个人资料(私隐)条例》
cards.en:
The Basic Law protects the freedom of speech but also restricts abuses of this freedom with laws (Table 2.3).
Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (個人資料(私隱)條例):
  • Definition: disclosing someone's personal data without their agreement with the intention to gain benefit or cause loss to that person.
  • Penalties: fines and imprisonment.
  • Applicable cases: doxxing, e.g. disclosing someone's mobile phone number; creating an account with someone's photos and personal information without permission.
Personal data includes name, ID number, phone number, address, photos that identify a person.
cards.zh:
《基本法》保障言论自由，但也有法例限制滥用。
《个人资料(私隐)条例》：
  • 定义：未经同意披露他人个人资料，意图获利或令该人受损。
  • 刑罚：罚款和监禁。
  • 适用情况：起底，如公开别人手机号码；未经允许用别人照片和资料开帐户。
个人资料包括姓名、身份证号、电话、地址、可识别人的照片。

ex.q: Jane creates a social media account with Amy's photos and personal information without permission. Which law may Jane violate?
ex.a: The Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance (using/disclosing Amy's personal data without consent). If she also posts false statements that harm Amy's reputation, the Defamation Ordinance. Copyright is not the main issue here. (Textbook Exercise MC12)
ex.az: 《个人资料(私隐)条例》。

cards.t: Legal consequences: Defamation and Theft Ordinances
cards.tz: 法律后果：《诽谤条例》与《盗窃罪条例》
cards.en:
Defamation Ordinance 誹謗條例Theft Ordinance 盜竊罪條例 (Blackmail and Fraud)
DefinitionPublishing information that harms someone's reputationBlackmail: demanding benefit from someone for not disclosing their information. Fraud: using false personal information to obtain property from someone
PenaltiesFines and imprisonmentImprisonment
Applicable casesReposting fake news which harms the reputation of an individual or a party; spreading false information about someone you hateBlackmail (勒索): demand money for not disclosing someone's personal information. Fraud (欺詐): use fake profiles to steal someone's money
Example: George posts Amy's phone number and photos (Privacy) and fake statements that she shoplifted (Defamation): violates (2) and (3), not Copyright.
cards.zh:
《诽谤条例》《盗窃罪条例》（勒索与欺诈）
定义发布损害他人名誉的资讯勒索：以不公开对方资料为条件索取利益。欺诈：用虚假个人资料骗取财物
刑罚罚款和监禁监禁
例子转发损害个人或团体名誉的假新闻；散播关于讨厌的人的假资讯索钱才不公开别人资料；用假帐户骗钱
例：George 公开 Amy 电话照片（私隐）并捏造她偷窃（诽谤）。

ex.q: Peter is hired to spread rumours on a forum which harm the reputation of a company. Which statement is correct?
ex.a: The company may take legal actions against Peter's behaviour (Defamation Ordinance). He has no right to spread false information. (Textbook Exercise MC5: C)
ex.az: 公司可以对 Peter 采取法律行动（诽谤）。

cards.en:
Abusing freedom of information includes scamming and social engineering (tricking people into giving information or money; Core C section 5.3).
Checkpoint example: George posts "I found a technical bug on an online shopping site! I got a $500 off coupon. Send a direct message to me and I will send you the method!" Amy does not repost it because (1) it may be a scam as George's identity is unknown, (2) it may cause a huge loss to that online shopping site, (3) it is illegal to steal coupons without authority.
Exercise example: an online friend Andy is asked by Amy to lend money for tuition. Andy's classmate disagrees because Amy may tell lies and it may be a fraud (Theft Ordinance: fraud).
cards.zh:
滥用资讯自由也包括诈骗和社交工程（骗人交出资料或金钱）。
例：George 声称发现购物网站漏洞可得 $500 优惠券，叫人私讯他。Amy 不转发因为：(1) George 身份不明，可能是骗局；(2) 会令网站蒙受巨大损失；(3) 未经授权盗用优惠券违法。
例：网友 Amy 向 Andy 借钱交学费，同学反对因为 Amy 可能说谎，可能是欺诈。

ex.q: Amy met Andy on a social networking site and asks him to lend money for tuition. Why should Andy not lend it?
ex.a: Andy only knows Amy online, so her identity and story cannot be verified; Amy may tell lies and it may be a fraud (social engineering). (Textbook Exercise MC6: C)
ex.az: 身份无法核实，可能是欺诈。

cards.t: Protecting personal data on social media
cards.tz: 在社交媒体保护个人资料
cards.en:
Personal data leakage often comes from what we post ourselves. Good practice:
  • Set the account to private and only allow close friends to see posts.
  • Do not post sensitive data (phone number, address, school, ID, location in real time).
  • Think before posting photos; once online they can be reposted to forums.
  • Check privacy settings of each app regularly.
Checkpoint example: Eva posted selfies with funny faces on a public account; they were reposted to a forum with teasing comments. Best prevention: set her account to private and only allow close friends to see it (not stop taking selfies or quit the Internet; commenting on the forum asking people to stop does not prevent leakage).
cards.zh:
个人资料外泄常来自我们自己发的内容：
  • 帐户设为私人，只让好友看。
  • 不发敏感资料（电话、地址、学校、实时位置）。
  • 发照片前想清楚，上网后可被转贴。
  • 定期检查私隐设定。
例：Eva 在公开帐户发鬼脸自拍，被转贴到论坛嘲笑。预防方法：设为私人，只让好友看。

ex.q: Eva's public selfies were reposted to a forum with teasing comments. How can she prevent personal data leakage?
ex.a: Set her account to private and only allow close friends to see it. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.3 Q4: B)
ex.az: 设为私人帐户。

cards.t: Digital equity and Internet penetration in Hong Kong
cards.tz: 数码平等与香港互联网普及率
cards.en:
Digital equity refers to the condition in which people have equitable access to technology to participate in modern society. (equity of access 公平存取)
Hong Kong has a relatively high Internet and device penetration rate (OGCIO, 2021):
  • Internet penetration in households: 94%
  • Smartphone penetration: 92.1%; personal computer: 75.3%
  • Mobile subscriber penetration: 292% (more than 2 subscriptions per person)
  • Usage of the Internet: 92%
Most people have used the Internet, but there are still issues of digital equity locally and globally. Historical note: the Internet could once only be accessed through computers; mobile devices changed the way we interact with society.
cards.zh:
Digital equity（数码平等）指人们能公平地取用科技、参与现代社会的状况。
香港普及率高（OGCIO 2021）：
  • 家庭上网：94%
  • 智能手机：92.1%；个人电脑：75.3%
  • 流动电话用户普及率：292%（每人超过两个号码）
  • 互联网使用率：92%
虽然大部分人用过互联网，本地和全球仍有数码平等问题。历史：以前只能用电脑上网，流动装置改变了我们与社会互动的方式。

ex.q: Explain how a mobile subscriber penetration of 292% is possible.
ex.a: Penetration = number of subscriptions ÷ population × 100%. Many people hold more than one SIM/subscription (e.g. a phone plus a tablet or a second number), so the total can exceed 100%: on average about 2.9 subscriptions per person.
ex.az: 每人可有多于一个号码，所以超过 100%。

cards.tz: 数码隔阂的意思与范畴
cards.en:
Digital divide describes the gap between individuals or groups of people in terms of:
Hardware and softwareInternet connectionICT skills and literacy
Necessary tools to use the technology
Quality
Localisation		Broadband and mobile network
Stability
Data transfer speed		Obtaining information
Processing information and creating new ideas
Lifelong learning
Impact: digital divide affects the connection between individuals and modern society. The individuals will be increasingly isolated from necessary daily services and become less competitive in the job market.
Example: shops closing and moving to e-commerce (Gap closed all HK stores in 2020) may create "abandoned malls" and leave people with low computer literacy unable to shop.
cards.zh:
Digital divide（数码隔阂）指个人或群体之间在以下方面的差距：
  • 硬件和软件：必要工具、质素、本地化
  • 互联网连接：宽带和流动网络、稳定性、传输速度
  • ICT 技能与素养：取得资讯、处理资讯并创造新想法、终身学习
影响：这些人会越来越与必要的日常服务隔绝，在就业市场竞争力下降。
例：零售商转向网购（Gap 2020 年关闭全港分店），电脑能力低的人难以购物。

ex.q: What is the problem of digital divide?
ex.a: Those who cannot access online information will become isolated from society (daily services, jobs). (Textbook Exercise MC4: A)
ex.az: 无法上网的人会被社会孤立。

cards.t: Causes: demographic factors (age, gender, race, ethnicity)
cards.en:
Digital divide occurs between demographic groups with regard to age, gender, race and ethnicity.
Aging problem: the elderly are less knowledgeable about using PCs and less likely to have smartphones, so they use online purchase and mobile payment services much less. (OGCIO 2021: PC skills young/middle-age 96% vs elderly 49%; smartphone 98% vs 68%.)
Gender gap: females show less interest and confidence in pursuing STEM because of the stereotypical belief that only boys have the inborn talent for STEM. Preference to study STEM at university: female 14%, male 40% (EdUHK 2018). Women are underrepresented in big tech: Apple total 34% / tech 24%; Google 33% / 26% (2020). Hedy Lamarr's "frequency hopping" inspired Wi-Fi, Bluetooth and GPS.
cards.zh:
数码隔阂出现在不同年龄、性别、种族、族裔的群体之间。
人口老化：长者较不懂用电脑、较少有智能手机，少用网购和流动支付（电脑技能：青壮年 96% vs 长者 49%；智能手机 98% vs 68%）。
性别差距：因为“只有男生有读 STEM 天分”的刻板印象，女性对 STEM 兴趣和信心较低。想读 STEM：女 14%，男 40%。大型科技公司女性比例：Apple 34%（技术岗 24%），Google 33%（26%）。Hedy Lamarr 的跳频技术启发了 Wi-Fi、蓝牙、GPS。

ex.q: Using the data, compare the digital divide between young and elderly people in Hong Kong.
ex.a: PC skills: 96% (young/middle-age) vs 49% (elderly), a gap of 47 percentage points. Smartphone penetration: 98% vs 68%, a gap of 30 points. So the elderly are much less able to use online shopping and mobile payment.
ex.az: 电脑技能差 47 个百分点，手机差 30 个百分点。

cards.en:
Three socioeconomic factors (OGCIO 2021 data):
  • Education: people with secondary and higher education have more chances to acquire advanced knowledge of technology. PC skills: primary 53%, secondary 96%, post-secondary 99%. Smartphone: 68% / 97% / 99%.
  • Household income: a huge gap between rich and poor; high-speed Internet, high-end devices and PCs are much less affordable to low-income households. Internet: <$10000 72% vs ≥$10000 99%. PC: 35% vs 85%.
  • Work status: economically active persons are more likely to learn and apply new technology; people may feel left out after retirement. PC skills 97% vs 53%; smartphone 99% vs 71%.
cards.zh:
社会经济因素：
  • 教育：中学及以上学历者较多机会学习科技。电脑技能：小学 53%、中学 96%、专上 99%。
  • 家庭收入：贫富差距大，低收入家庭难负担高速网络和电脑。上网：月入<$10000 72% vs ≥$10000 99%；电脑 35% vs 85%。
  • 工作状况：在职人士更会学用新科技，退休后可能被社会遗下。电脑技能 97% vs 53%。

ex.q: PC penetration is 35% for households earning under $10000 and 85% for those earning $10000 or more. How many times more likely is a higher-income household to own a PC? Explain the cause.
ex.a: 85 ÷ 35 ≈ 2.4 times. Cause: PCs and high-speed broadband are less affordable for low-income households (household income factor).
ex.az: 约 2.4 倍，因为低收入家庭负担不起。

cards.en:
The infrastructure (free Wi-Fi hotspots, broadband, mobile network) differs greatly between locations.
Urban and rural areas: cities have higher population density and more potential customers, so infrastructure is already there and only needs improvement; it is more affordable and easier to catch up on new technology. People in the countryside face higher prices for new technology because of high infrastructure cost and less price competition.
Developing and developed countries: the gap is due to national economies and education conditions. Also, people who speak only local languages face difficulties because less localised and translated content is provided: about 7000 languages and dialects but only 12 in use online; website content English 61% vs Chinese 1.4%. Minority language speakers may only use technology in their second language (Fig. 2.19).
cards.zh:
基建（免费 Wi-Fi、宽带、流动网络）因地区而异。
城乡：城市人口密度高、潜在客户多，基建已有，较便宜容易追上新科技；乡郊因基建成本高、价格竞争少，新科技较贵。
发展中与已发展国家：差距源于国家经济和教育条件。只懂本地语言的人因本地化和翻译内容少而难取资讯：约 7000 种语言方言，网上常用只有 12 种；网站内容英文 61%、中文 1.4%。

ex.q: Why is high-speed Internet more expensive in rural areas?
ex.a: Low population density means fewer customers to share the high cost of building infrastructure, and there are fewer providers so less price competition.
ex.az: 基建成本高、客户少、竞争少。

cards.en:
People with disabilities have lower skills and access to the Internet less often. Types: visual impairment (視覺障礙), hearing impairment (聽覺障礙), physical disability (肢體殘障) and cognitive impairment (認知障礙).
  • Website and software accessibility: only a few private websites and new technologies consider accessibility, creating a barrier to disabled people in the digital society. (Hong Kong: 100% of government websites and apps are disabled-accessible, 2018.)
  • Extra cost for assistive technology: besides normal hardware/Internet costs, the disabled need assistive devices or software continuously; many are expensive, and the user experience is still limited by content design.
Example: Professor Stephen Hawking used muscle sensors and specific software to control the computer and speak (ACAT, released as open source).
cards.zh:
残疾人士技能较低、较少上网。类型：视觉障碍、听觉障碍、肢体残障、认知障碍。
  • 网站和软件无障碍：只有少数私营网站和新科技考虑无障碍，形成障碍。（香港政府网站和 app 100% 无障碍）
  • 辅助科技的额外成本：除一般费用外还要长期购买辅助装置/软件，很多都昂贵，内容设计也限制用户体验。
例：霍金用肌肉感应器和专门软件控制电脑及说话（ACAT 已开源）。

ex.q: State TWO reasons why disabled people are on the wrong side of the digital divide.
ex.a:
1. Many private websites/software are not accessible (e.g. no alt text, poor contrast), creating barriers.
2. They must pay extra costs for assistive technology (e.g. braille display), which is expensive.
ex.az: 网站不无障碍；辅助科技贵。

cards.en:
If we ignore the gap, it will only become wider. To bridge the digital divide, measures are needed in several sectors. The HK government spent about HK$10,721 million on ICT in 2019-2020 (OGCIO).
Government support and promotion:
  • Provide free Wi-Fi hotspots and IT facilities in public spaces.
  • Subsidise needy students from low-income families to acquire hardware, software and Internet access.
  • Provide funding for enhancing schools' IT and Wi-Fi infrastructure.
  • Expand fibre-based network coverage to old buildings and remote areas (5G).
  • Fund the development of accessible apps and websites.
  • Organise recognition schemes to encourage digital inclusion.
cards.zh:
忽视差距只会令它越来越大。香港政府 2019-20 年 ICT 开支约 107.21 亿港元。
政府支持和推广：
  • 公共地方提供免费 Wi-Fi 和 IT 设施。
  • 资助低收入家庭学生购买硬件、软件和上网。
  • 资助学校提升 IT 和 Wi-Fi 基建。
  • 把光纤网络扩展到旧楼和偏远地区（5G）。
  • 资助开发无障碍 app 和网站。
  • 举办嘉许计划鼓励数码共融。

ex.q: Ben grew up in a poor countryside family with poor Internet. Suggest TWO government measures to help poor people in the countryside.
ex.a:
1. Expand fibre-based network / 5G coverage to remote areas.
2. Subsidise low-income families to buy computers and Internet access (or provide free Wi-Fi hotspots and IT facilities in public places).
ex.az: 扩展光纤到偏远地区；资助购买电脑和上网。

cards.en:
To ensure students and people with low IT literacy receive high-quality IT education, it is important to train educators as well:
  • Provide support for parenting in the digital age, e.g. parenting app and IT training.
  • Prepare teachers for online teaching and technology skills.
  • Launch Internet learning support programmes for people who lack basic IT skills.
Elderly examples: an Elderly IT Learning Portal to share skills online; an ICT Outreach Programme to teach the elderly basic IT skills. (An advanced ICT course does not target the elderly's basic-skill gap.)
Gender example: Girls Go Tech (The Women's Foundation) encourages underprivileged girls into STEM through workshops (Hackathon, AI Experience Workshop) and career talks; this builds interest and confidence and breaks stereotypes.
cards.zh:
确保学生和资讯素养低的人得到优质教育，也要培训教育者：
  • 支援数码时代育儿（育儿 app、IT 训练）。
  • 培训老师网上教学和科技技能。
  • 为缺乏基本 IT 技能者推出网上学习支援计划。
长者：长者 IT 学习网站、ICT 外展计划教基本技能（进阶课程不对症）。
性别：Girls Go Tech（妇女基金会）以工作坊（黑客松、AI 体验）及职业讲座鼓励基层女生读 STEM，建立兴趣信心、打破刻板印象。

ex.q: How does Girls Go Tech bridge the gender digital divide?
ex.a: It lets underprivileged girls experience new technology through hackathons and AI workshops, building interest and confidence, and its career talks give information on STEM careers, challenging the stereotype that only boys are good at STEM. More girls then choose STEM studies and careers.
ex.az: 工作坊建立兴趣信心，讲座提供 STEM 出路资讯，打破刻板印象。

cards.tz: 为残疾人士设计的辅助科技
cards.en:
Assistive technology is any device, software, or equipment designed to overcome the physical barrier. It allows the disabled to browse the Internet and use other digital devices equally.
TechnologyHow it helps
Braille display device 點字顯示器displays output from PC/mobile devices in braille characters by raising dots (visually impaired)
Screen reader / Voice-over and digital assistantcontent on the screen is described in speech; users control the device by voice or type with speech-to-text (visually and physically impaired)
Video call and live captioncamera lets hearing impaired people use sign language; live captions display speech or sound as text
Live transcribespeech converted into text in real time by speech recognition
Closed captioningsubtitles including dialogue and non-speech audio information, shown with the video
cards.zh:
辅助科技是任何为克服身体障碍而设计的装置、软件或设备，让残疾人士能平等上网和使用数码装置。
  • 点字显示器：以凸起的点显示点字（视障）。
  • 读屏软件/Voice-over、数码助理：把屏幕内容读出来；用声音控制或语音转文字输入（视障、肢体残障）。
  • 视像通话与实时字幕：听障人士用手语沟通；实时字幕把语音显示为文字。
  • Live transcribe 实时转录：用语音识别即时把说话转成文字。
  • Closed captioning 隐藏式字幕：包括对白和非语音声音资讯。

ex.q: Which feature helps visually impaired people use ICT: multilingual content / live transcription / closed captions / screen reader and braille display?
ex.a: Screen reader and braille display. Live transcription and closed captions help hearing impaired people; multilingual content helps ethnic minorities. (Textbook Exercise MC3: D)
ex.az: 读屏和点字显示器。

cards.en:
The HK government issued an accessibility handbook with guidelines for web and app design; GovHK provides information in ethnic minority languages.
  • Multi-language: ethnic minorities can use online services without knowing Chinese or English (e.g. Hindi, Bahasa Indonesia, Nepali).
  • High contrast version: people with colour blindness (e.g. protanopia, deuteranopia, tritanopia) find it hard to distinguish elements if colours are too similar.
  • Alternative text (alt text): describes an image in text (e.g. "The sun is above a mountain") so that screen readers can read it to visually impaired users.
Other features (EOC website): text size buttons (A A A), sitemap, mobile version, language switch, search. Video sites: captions, adjustable playback speed, audio description, keyboard shortcuts.
cards.zh:
政府发出无障碍网页手册，GovHK 提供少数族裔语言资讯。
  • 多语言：少数族裔不懂中英文也能用网上服务。
  • 高对比版本：色盲人士难以分辨颜色相近的元素。
  • 替代文字 alt text：用文字描述图片，让读屏软件读给视障者听。
其他：字体大小按钮、网站地图、流动版、语言切换、搜寻。影片网站：字幕、可调速度、口述影像、快捷键。

ex.q: Ben has mild colour blindness. How can the company help him use the computer more easily?
ex.a: Use a high contrast theme / colour-blind display mode (or adjust colour settings) so that elements are distinguished by strong contrast rather than similar colours.
ex.az: 使用高对比主题或色盲模式。

cards.tz: 智能手机的无障碍功能
cards.en:
Activity 2.7 features built into most smartphones:
  • Screen reader / Voice-over: content on screen is described in speech; tap to hear an option, double tap to select.
  • Live transcribe: real-time speech-to-text.
  • Closed captioning: subtitles automatically shown with videos.
  • Digital assistant: carries out voice commands such as phone calls, schedules, searching.
Advantages of a live transcription app (Checkpoint 2.5): makes communication between hearing impaired people and the world easier; jots notes in meetings and lessons automatically; reduces RSI by reducing keyboard use. It narrows (not widens) the digital divide.
For a 70-year-old father with a tablet: make the font bigger and install a simple and clean launcher.
cards.zh:
Activity 2.7 手机内置功能：
  • 读屏/Voice-over：屏幕内容读出来，单击听选项、双击选择。
  • Live transcribe：实时语音转文字。
  • Closed captioning：影片自动显示字幕。
  • 数码助理：以语音指令打电话、管理日程、搜寻。
实时转录 app 的好处：听障者与外界沟通更容易；自动记笔记；减少打字从而减少 RSI。它缩窄而非扩大数码隔阂。
给 70 岁父亲的平板：放大字体、安装简洁启动器。

ex.q: Susan buys a tablet for her 70-year-old father. Which actions should she do? (1) buy a wireless mouse (2) make the font bigger (3) enable screen reader (4) install a simple and clean launcher
ex.a: (2) and (4) only: bigger font for weaker eyesight and a simple launcher to reduce memory load. He is not described as blind, so a screen reader is unnecessary. (Textbook Exercise MC10: D)

cards.t: Misconception: digital divide only means no Internet
cards.tz: 误解：数码隔阂只是没有网络
cards.en:
Wrong: "Hong Kong has 94% household Internet penetration, so there is no digital divide."
Correct: digital divide covers three aspects: hardware and software (quality, localisation), Internet connection (stability, speed) and ICT skills and literacy. Someone with a phone and Internet but who cannot use online banking or judge fake news is still on the wrong side. Gaps exist by age, education, income, work status, location and disability.
Wrong: "Going fully digital (e.g. only accepting digital payment for government services) helps everyone." It actually widens the divide for the elderly and low-income groups. Good measures keep alternatives and add support.
cards.zh:
错误：“香港家庭上网率 94%，所以没有数码隔阂。”
正确：数码隔阂包括硬件软件（质素、本地化）、网络连接（稳定、速度）和 ICT 技能素养。有手机有网但不会网上理财或分辨假新闻，仍然处于劣势。差距按年龄、教育、收入、工作、地区、残疾存在。
错误：“政府服务只收电子支付能帮所有人。”这会扩大长者和低收入人士的隔阂。

ex.q: Which measures help overcome the digital divide? (1) more free Wi-Fi (2) fund the disabled to buy smartphones with assistive technology (3) high-contrast official websites (4) abandon cash and only accept digital payment
ex.a: (1), (2) and (3) only. (4) excludes people without digital payment skills or devices, widening the divide. (Textbook Exercise MC8: C)

cards.en:
Our life is flooded with electronic gadgets because of rapid technological development. Eager to follow the trend, we often buy new products to replace old ones even when they are still functioning. The disposed products become electronic waste (e-waste). In 2019, 53.6 million tonnes of e-waste were produced globally.
E-waste contains toxic substances such as lead (鉛), mercury (水銀) and brominated flame retardants (溴化阻燃劑). Once these leak into soil or rivers, the ecosystem and residents' health are seriously affected.
Hong Kong: the WEEE (四電一腦) recycling scheme provides a free recycling service; citizens can request free door-to-door removal by statutory recyclers after buying air-conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, TVs, computers, printers, scanners or monitors.
cards.zh:
科技发展快，我们常在旧产品仍能用时就换新，丢弃的产品成为电子废物。2019 年全球产生 5360 万吨。
电子废物含铅、水银、溴化阻燃剂等有毒物质，渗入泥土河流会严重影响生态和居民健康。
香港 WEEE「四电一脑」回收计划：免费回收；购买冷气机、雪柜、洗衣机、电视、电脑、打印机、扫描器、显示器后可要求法定回收商免费上门收旧机。

ex.q: Ben's company throws away many old electric appliances every year. Suggest TWO measures to protect the environment.
ex.a:
1. Send them to the WEEE (四電一腦) recycling scheme / statutory recyclers instead of dumping.
2. Repair, reuse or donate appliances that still work, and avoid replacing products that are still functioning (3R).
(Also: turn off computers after work / use power-saving settings.)
ex.az: 交四电一脑回收；维修、再用或捐赠。

cards.en:
The popularisation of electronic products makes life convenient but increases energy consumption. Because of the limited energy reserves on Earth, high energy consumption not only intensifies the energy shortage but also brings greater harm to nature during resource extraction (能源開採).
EnergyOilNatural gasUranium ore (nuclear)Coal ore
Years before depletion40-5060-7060-70200-300
(Source: World Energy Council, 2013.) Oil will run out first.
Simple saving actions: turn off computers after work; battery optimisation; dark mode on OLED screens; lower screen brightness; close unused apps/tabs.
cards.zh:
电子产品普及令能源消耗增加。由于地球能源储量有限，高耗能不但加剧能源短缺，开采资源时也更破坏大自然。
能源石油天然气铀矿（核能）煤
耗尽年数40-5060-7060-70200-300
石油最先耗尽。
节能：下班关电脑、电池优化、OLED 用深色模式、降低亮度、关闭不用的 app/分页。

ex.q: According to Table 2.4, which energy source will be depleted first, and roughly when (from 2013)?
ex.a: Oil, in 40-50 years, i.e. around 2053-2063.

cards.t: Energy labels (Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme)
cards.tz: 能源标签（强制性能源效益标签计划）
cards.en:
Since 2009, the Electrical and Mechanical Services Department (EMSD) has implemented the Mandatory Energy Efficiency Labelling Scheme (強制性能源效益標籤計劃). Energy labels must be stuck on prescribed products supplied in Hong Kong, to help citizens distinguish products' energy efficiency and raise awareness of saving energy.
Labels have five grades: Grade 1 (green) consumes the least energy, Grade 2 next, and so on to Grade 5. Example: an air-conditioner with a Grade 1 label can save 43% of electricity compared with a Grade 5 one. The label also shows annual energy consumption (kWh).
Appliances with labels: air-conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, dehumidifiers, televisions, etc.
cards.zh:
自 2009 年，机电工程署 (EMSD) 推行强制性能源效益标签计划：指定产品在港出售须贴能源标签，帮市民分辨能源效益、提高节能意识。
标签分五级：1 级（绿色）最省电，依次到 5 级。例：1 级冷气机比 5 级省电 43%。标签亦显示每年耗电量（kWh）。
有标签的电器：冷气机、雪柜、洗衣机、抽湿机、电视等。

cards.t: Positive impact: smart use of electricity
cards.en:
Apart from changing habits, technology helps us use energy more efficiently, reducing consumption and helping achieve sustainable development.
Smart use of electricity: with the Internet of Things and smart cities, machines combine sensors and artificial intelligence to provide real-time information and adjust operation modes to reduce waste.
  • Real-time Adaptive Traffic Signal System (實時交通燈號調節系統): adjusts green times according to real-time traffic and pedestrian flow, reducing waiting time and relieving congestion.
  • Smart meters monitor electricity use.
  • Smart parking metres with e-payment and real-time vacant-space data reduce car exhaust from drivers circling for parking.
  • Free-Flow Tolling: no stopping at toll booths, saving manpower, improving traffic, reducing carbon emission.

智能用电：物联网和智慧城市中，机器结合感应器与人工智能提供实时资讯并调整运作，减少浪费。
  • 实时交通灯号调节系统：按实时车流人流调整绿灯时间，减少等候和挤塞。
  • 智能电表监察用电。
  • 智能咪表：电子支付+实时空位资料，减少司机兜圈找车位的废气。
  • 不停车缴费：节省人手、改善交通、减少碳排放。

ex.q: The government installs parking metres with e-payment and real-time vacant space data. What is the purpose?
ex.a: To reduce car exhaust emission when drivers are looking for parking spaces: drivers go straight to a vacant space instead of circling around. (Textbook Checkpoint 2.6 Q2: A)
ex.az: 减少司机找车位时的废气排放。

cards.t: Positive impact: pollution monitoring, carbon footprint, going paperless
cards.tz: 正面影响：污染监测、减碳、无纸化
cards.en:
• Pollution monitoring: IT monitors environmental changes so timely adjustments can be made. In Hong Kong, remote sensing devices monitor air pollution and unmanned vessels (無人船隻) monitor water quality in reservoirs (e.g. Plover Cove).
  • Reduction of carbon footprint: companies, schools and government can implement work from home and video conferences, saving travelling time and reducing energy consumption and CO₂ emission.
  • Going paperless: digitalise paper documents (e-books, e-statements, e-learning). Enables convenient management, storage and searching, and protects the ecosystem by reducing paper use. (In 2021, printer paper production in major countries fell 20-30% year on year.)
Protecting the environment: 3Rs: Reduce, Reuse, Recycle; stakeholders: government, businesses, citizens.
cards.zh:
• 污染监测：香港用遥感装置监测空气污染，无人船监测水塘水质（如船湾淡水湖）。
  • 减少碳足迹：推行在家工作和视像会议，节省交通、减少耗能和二氧化碳排放。
  • 无纸化：电子书、电子月结单、电子学习；方便管理、储存、搜寻，减少用纸保护生态。（2021 年主要国家打印纸产量按年跌 20-30%）
环保 3R：Reduce 减少使用、Reuse 物尽其用、Recycle 循环再造；持份者：政府、企业、市民。

ex.q: Suggest TWO ways each for government, businesses and citizens to protect the environment with respect to technology.
ex.a:
Government: run e-waste (WEEE) recycling; mandatory energy labels / smart traffic systems.
Businesses: work-from-home and video conferencing; go paperless with e-statements.
Citizens: buy Grade 1 appliances; repair/reuse devices instead of replacing working ones.
ex.az: 政府：回收计划、能源标签；企业：视像会议、电子月结单；市民：买一级电器、维修再用。

cards.en:
Practical ways to make a phone or laptop use less electricity:
  • Turn on battery optimisation / power-saving mode.
  • Lower screen brightness or use auto-brightness; shorter automatic screen lock time.
  • Dark mode on OLED screens: each OLED pixel emits light independently, and black pixels do not emit light and consume no power.
  • Close unused apps and browser tabs; turn off Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/GPS when not needed.
  • Reduce screen resolution or refresh rate.
Exam trap: turning off the automatic screen lock or opening tens of browser tabs wastes power. Note dark mode saves energy on OLED, not much on LCD (LCD backlight is always on).
cards.zh:
手机/电脑省电方法：
  • 开启电池优化/省电模式。
  • 降低亮度；缩短自动锁屏时间。
  • OLED 屏幕用深色模式：每个 OLED 像素独立发光，黑色像素不发光、不耗电。
  • 关闭不用的 app 和分页；不用时关 Wi-Fi/蓝牙/GPS。
  • 降低分辨率或刷新率。
陷阱：关闭自动锁屏、开几十个分页都是浪费电。深色模式对 OLED 有效，对 LCD 作用不大（背光常亮）。
