cards.en:
Intellectual Property (IP) means the creation of intellect. It is usually used to represent a set of separate intangible asset rights granted to a person, a party, or a company. 'Intangible' means you cannot touch the asset itself: you own the right to a song, a design or an invention, not just the physical CD or phone.

Why protect IP? Respecting and protecting the ownership of every creation ensures a safe and fair environment for artists and inventors to continue their innovations. If anyone could copy freely, creators would lose income and motivation.

Key points to memorise:
  • IP = creation of intellect; a set of separate intangible asset rights.
  • Rights can belong to an individual, a group (party) or a company.
  • Four main types: copyright, patent, trademark, registered design.
Chapter opener (Activity 3.1): downloading a movie from a paid subscription site such as Netflix is legal; redistributing a copyrighted app to a friend through instant messaging, or photocopying an entire borrowed textbook to save money, is not.
cards.zh:
知识产权 Intellectual Property (IP) 指 the creation of intellect（智力创作）。它通常代表 a set of separate intangible asset rights（一组独立的无形财产权）granted to a person, a party, or a company。“无形”是指你拥有的是对歌曲、设计或发明的权利，而不只是实体CD或手机。

为什么要保护？尊重并保护每件创作的拥有权，可以 ensure a safe and fair environment for artists and inventors to continue their innovations。如果人人都可随意复制，创作者会失去收入和动力。

要背：
  • IP = creation of intellect，是一组无形财产权。
  • 权利可属于个人、团体或公司。
  • 四大类：copyright、patent、trademark、registered design。
Activity 3.1：在 Netflix 等付费订阅平台下载电影是合法的；用即时通讯把付费 app 转给朋友、影印整本借来的课本都是违法的。

ex.q: A student downloads a movie for offline viewing from a paid YouTube Premium account, and also sends a paid app's installation file to a friend via WhatsApp. Which act is legal?
ex.a: The download is legal because it is done through the platform's subscription service under its terms of use. Sending the app file is unauthorised redistribution of a copyrighted work, which infringes copyright.
ex.az: 订阅平台内的离线下载符合使用条款，合法；把付费 app 文件转发给朋友属于未经授权的分发，侵犯版权。

cards.t: Four types of IP: overview and registration
cards.en:
There are four main types of intellectual property rights:
TypeProtectsExample
CopyrightThe right given to the owner of an original workComputer software, sound recording, film
PatentInventions: a product, process or substanceFacebook's dynamic mask application
TrademarkA unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'Logo, slogan, app name, app icon
Registered designNew and distinctive appearance of productsMobile phone's appearance, GUI
Key exam point: Except for copyright, the other types of IP all require registration. Copyright arises automatically when the work is created; patents, trademarks and registered designs must be registered (in Hong Kong, through the Intellectual Property Department) before you get protection.
cards.zh:
知识产权有四大类：
  • 版权 Copyright：给予独创作品拥有者的权利，例如电脑软件、录音、电影。
  • 专利 Patent：保护发明，可以是产品 product、方法 process 或物质 substance，例如 Facebook 的动态面具功能。
  • 商标 Trademark：a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'，例如标志、口号、app 名称和图标。
  • 注册外观设计 Registered design：保护产品新颖而独特的外观，例如手机外形、图形用户界面。
考试重点：Except for copyright, the other types of IP all require registration. 版权在作品完成时自动产生；专利、商标、注册外观设计都必须注册（香港由知识产权署处理）才受保护。

ex.q: A start-up invents a new battery-charging method, names its product 'ZapGo', and writes the control software. Which IP right protects each, and which need registration?
ex.a:
Charging method → patent (needs registration).
Name 'ZapGo' → trademark (needs registration).
Control software → copyright (automatic, no registration).
ex.az: 充电方法→专利（需注册）；名称→商标（需注册）；软件→版权（自动，毋须注册）。

cards.t: Copyright symbol and patents for software
cards.en:
Copyright is the right given to the owner of an original work. Owners often show it with the copyright symbol ©, followed by the owner and year, e.g. © Eva Chan 2020 or © John Smith / Hong Kong Press. Typical copyrighted works in ICT: computer software, sound recordings, films.

Patent is protection of inventions which can be a product, process (方法) or substance (物質). A common misunderstanding is that software can only be protected by copyright. In fact, computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem. Examples given: Facebook's dynamic mask application and Airbnb's automated determination of booking availability for user-sourced accommodations.

Difference to remember: copyright protects the code as written (the expression); a patent protects the technical method or invention, even if someone writes different code to do the same thing. A patent must be registered; copyright need not be.
cards.zh:
版权 Copyright 是给予独创作品拥有者的权利，常用 © 加拥有者和年份表示，如 © Eva Chan 2020、© John Smith / Hong Kong Press。ICT 常见版权作品：电脑软件、录音、电影。

专利 Patent 保护发明（产品、方法或物质）。常见误解是软件只受版权保护；其实 computer programs can be patented if they solve a technical problem。课本例子：Facebook 的 dynamic mask 功能、Airbnb 自动判断房源可订状态。

分别：版权保护写出来的代码本身（表达）；专利保护技术方法或发明，即使别人用不同代码实现同一方法也可能侵权。专利要注册，版权不用。

ex.q: Company A copies none of Company B's code but re-implements B's patented automatic booking-availability method. Can B take action? Under which right?
ex.a: Yes, under the patent. Copyright would not help because no code was copied, but the patent protects the technical method itself, so re-implementing it without a licence infringes the patent.
ex.az: 可以，依据专利。没抄代码所以版权帮不上，但专利保护的是技术方法本身。

cards.tz: 商标（™ 与 ®）及注册外观设计
cards.en:
Trademark: a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'. Examples of application: logo, slogan, app name, app icon. Two symbols:
  • ™: trademark, used to claim a sign as your brand (often not yet registered).
  • ®: registered trademark, only allowed after official registration.
Registered design: protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products, i.e. how a product looks, not how it works. Examples: a mobile phone's appearance and a graphical user interface (GUI).

Don't mix them up:
  • Logo of a phone brand → trademark (identifies the source).
  • Shape/curves of the phone body → registered design (appearance).
  • The display technology inside → patent (invention).
  • Source code of the phone's OS → copyright (original work).
This smartphone mapping is Activity 3.2 in the book and a classic exam question.
cards.zh:
商标 Trademark：a unique sign that distinguishes one's products or services from others'。例子：标志 logo、口号 slogan、app 名称、app 图标。两个符号：
  • ™：商标，表示声称这是自己的品牌（通常未注册）。
  • ®：注册商标，正式注册后才可使用。
注册外观设计 Registered design：protection of the new and distinctive appearance of products，保护产品的“样子”而不是功能。例子：手机外观、图形用户界面 GUI。

智能手机对照（Activity 3.2，常考）：
  • 品牌标志 → 商标
  • 机身外形 → 注册外观设计
  • 显示技术 → 专利
  • 源代码 → 版权

ex.q: For the 'ORANGE' smartphone, match each item to an IP right: (1) display technology (2) logo (3) appearance (4) source code.
ex.a: (1) Patent (2) Trademark (3) Registered design (4) Copyright.
ex.az: (1)专利 (2)商标 (3)注册外观设计 (4)版权。

cards.t: Who owns copyright? Monkey selfie and AI works
cards.tz: 谁拥有版权？猴子自拍与 AI 作品
cards.en:
Application and career case: Who owns copyright? In 2014 a monkey took selfie photos with a British photographer's camera. People argued whether the photographer or the monkey owned the copyright. The court affirmed that only works created by a human are protected under the Copyright Act. The monkey is only an animal, so its photos are in the public domain (no one owns copyright; anyone may use them).

The book then asks open questions: if an AI analyses the writing style of online newspapers and writes a news article, or creates music, who owns the copyright: the AI, the programmer, the owners of the input material, or nobody (public domain)?

Exam approach for such 'discuss' questions:
  • State the principle: copyright protects original works by a human author.
  • Consider the human contribution (programmer/user who directs the work).
  • Consider whether input works were used without permission (possible infringement).
  • Conclude with a reasoned view; no single fixed answer in the book.
cards.zh:
谁拥有版权？2014 年一只猴子用英国摄影师的相机自拍，引发版权归属争议。法院确认 only works created by a human are protected under the Copyright Act（只有人类创作的作品受保护）。猴子是动物，所以照片属于公共领域 public domain，没人拥有版权，任何人都可使用。

课本追问：如果 AI 分析网上报章写作风格后写出新闻、或 AI 作曲，版权属于 AI、程序员、输入歌曲的版权持有人，还是公共领域？

答这类讨论题的方法：
  • 先写原则：版权保护人类作者的独创作品。
  • 考虑人类贡献（程序员或下指令的用户）。
  • 考虑输入素材是否未经授权使用（可能侵权）。
  • 给出有理由的结论；课本没有唯一答案。

ex.q: Why could anyone legally use the monkey selfie in a school poster?
ex.a: The court held that only works created by humans are protected by copyright. The monkey is not a human, so the photo has no copyright owner and is in the public domain; using it needs no permission.
ex.az: 法院裁定只有人类作品受版权保护，照片属公共领域，使用毋须许可。

cards.en:
The copyright of a piece of work is automatically given to the author or creator after the work is completed. In Hong Kong, all creations are automatically protected by the legal system, so there is no need to register for copyright. In general, copyright lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator.

Consequences you should be able to explain:
  • A student who writes an essay or takes a photo owns its copyright immediately, even without writing '©' or 'All rights reserved'.
  • Putting a copyright notice is good practice but not legally required.
  • After copyright expires (e.g. music written in 1866), the work enters the public domain and can be copied freely.
Checkpoint 3.1: Cindy uploads photos without a watermark '© All rights reserved'. Correct statement: Cindy owns the copyright without declaration. The social media company does not become the owner, and she need not register.
cards.zh:
The copyright of a piece of work is automatically given to the author or creator after the work is completed. 在香港，所有创作自动受法律保护，毋须注册版权。一般而言，copyright lasts until 50 years after the death of the creator（作者死后 50 年）。

要会解释：
  • 学生写好文章或拍好照片，立即拥有版权，即使没有写“©”或“All rights reserved”。
  • 加版权声明是好习惯，但法律上不是必须。
  • 版权到期后（如 1866 年写的乐谱），作品进入公共领域，可自由复制。
Checkpoint 3.1：Cindy 上载照片没加水印，正确说法是 Cindy owns the copyright without declaration；社交平台不会因此拥有版权，她也毋须注册。

ex.q: A composer died in 1990. Roughly until when is his music protected by copyright in general?
ex.a: Copyright generally lasts until 50 years after the creator's death: 1990 + 50 = 2040. After that it enters the public domain.

cards.t: Works protected by the Copyright Ordinance
cards.en:
The Hong Kong Copyright Ordinance (版權條例) protects three groups of works:
WorksExamples
Original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic worksComputer programs, databases, photographs, essays, lyrics
Sound recordings, broadcasts, films, or cable programmesSongs, vlogs, movies, TV shows
The typographical arrangement (排印編排) of published editionsInterface layout of a published website, typographical arrangement of novels
Note for ICT students: computer programs and databases are protected as literary works. Even the layout of a published web page or book is protected separately from the words in it.

Not protected by copyright: ideas themselves (only their expression), and works not created by humans.
cards.zh:
香港《版权条例》Copyright Ordinance 保护三类作品：
  • Original literary, dramatic, musical or artistic works（独创文学、戏剧、音乐、艺术作品）：电脑程序、数据库、照片、文章、歌词。
  • Sound recordings, broadcasts, films, or cable programmes（录音、广播、电影、有线节目）：歌曲、vlog、电影、电视节目。
  • The typographical arrangement of published editions（已发表版本的排印编排）：已发布网站的界面排版、小说的排版。
ICT 重点：电脑程序和数据库属文学作品受保护；网页或书本的排版本身也另受保护。

不受版权保护：意念本身（只保护表达）、非人类创作的作品。

ex.q: Classify: (a) a mobile game's source code (b) a YouTube vlog (c) the page layout of a published e-book.
ex.a: (a) Original literary work (computer program). (b) Film/sound recording category. (c) Typographical arrangement of a published edition.
ex.az: (a)文学作品 (b)影片/录音类 (c)排印编排。

cards.tz: 误解：意念 vs 表达
cards.en:
Misconception: 'Ideas are protected by copyright.' Wrong.

Copyright does not protect ideas. It protects the expression of ideas when it is presented in a tangible form. For example, copyright does not protect the idea of taking sunset pictures, but it does protect Cindy's actual sunset photos, the tangible expression of that idea.

Applying this in ICT:
  • The idea of a 'to-do list app' is free for anyone; copying another app's actual source code or icons is infringement.
  • An algorithm idea described in words is not copyright protected, but the specific program code is (a technical method may still be patentable if registered).
Also from Checkpoint 3.1: the platform you upload to does not own your work; you keep copyright without any declaration.
cards.zh:
误解：“意念受版权保护。”错。

Copyright does not protect ideas. It protects the expression of ideas when it is presented in a tangible form. 例如“拍日落照”这个意念不受保护，但 Cindy 实际拍下的日落照片（有形表达）受保护。

ICT 应用：
  • “待办清单 app”这个想法人人可做；抄别人 app 的源代码或图标就侵权。
  • 用文字描述的算法意念不受版权保护，具体程序代码则受保护（技术方法注册后可另受专利保护）。

ex.q: Tom sees a popular note app and writes his own note app from scratch with similar features but his own code and icons. Is this copyright infringement?
ex.a: No. The idea/features of a note app are not protected by copyright; only the expression (code, graphics, text) is. Tom wrote his own code and icons, so he has not copied any protected expression (unless a patent or registered design is involved).
ex.az: 不是。功能意念不受版权保护，Tom 没抄代码和图像。

cards.en:
In Hong Kong, the owner of the copyright has exclusive rights, including but not limited to:
  1. Copy, publish, broadcast, adapt and translate the work.
  2. Grant the right to use the copyrighted work in return for royalties (版權費) or other payments.
  3. Sell the copyright.
  4. Pass the copyright to others in a will.
If a person uses your copyrighted work without your permission, you have the right to initiate legal action against the copyright infringement and obtain monetary compensation.

Exam tips:
  • 'Exclusive' means only the owner (or someone the owner authorises) may do these acts.
  • Copyright can be transferred (sold, inherited), so 'copyright owners cannot transfer their copyrights' is false.
  • Licensing software for a fee = granting the right to use in return for payment.
cards.zh:
在香港，版权拥有者享有专有权利 exclusive rights，包括但不限于：
  1. 复制、出版、广播、改编及翻译作品。
  2. Grant the right to use 作品，以换取版权费 royalties或其他报酬。
  3. 出售版权。
  4. 在遗嘱中把版权传给他人。
如有人未经许可使用你的作品，你有权 initiate legal action against the copyright infringement and obtain monetary compensation。

考试提示：版权可以转让（出售、继承），所以“拥有者不能转让版权”是错的；收牌照费授权软件 = 收费授予使用权。

ex.q: Peter writes a program by himself. Which are his rights? (1) Translate and publish it in another language (2) Charge users a licence fee (3) Sell the copyright to a company (4) Transfer ownership to others
ex.a: All four. (1) adapt/translate/publish; (2) grant right to use for royalties/payment; (3) sell copyright; (4) transfer, e.g. pass in will. (Textbook Ch3 Exercise MC9: answer D.)
ex.az: 四项都是他的权利。

cards.en:
The Creative Commons (CC, 共享創意授權條款) Licences are established to protect both creators and users. Creators put the CC logo next to their works to show which licence they adopt, so users know what they may do without asking each time.

The 4 CC elements:
  • Attribution (BY): you must give credit to the creator.
  • Share-alike (SA): if you adapt the work, you must share your new work under the same licence.
  • Non-commercial (NC): no commercial use.
  • No Derivative Works (ND): you may not modify/adapt it; share only the original unchanged.
They combine, e.g. CC BY-SA 2.0, CC BY-ND, CC BY-NC. A CC licence does not remove copyright: the creator still owns it and grants some rights ('Some rights reserved').
cards.zh:
创用 CC 授权 Creative Commons Licences 用来 protect both creators and users。创作者在作品旁放 CC 标志，表明采用哪种授权，用户便知道可以怎样使用，毋须每次询问。

四个元素：
  • BY 署名：必须注明作者。
  • SA 相同方式分享：改编后的作品须用同一授权分享。
  • NC 非商业：不可作商业用途。
  • ND 禁止改作：不可修改，只能原样分享。
可组合，如 CC BY-SA 2.0、CC BY-ND。CC 不会取消版权：作者仍拥有版权，只是开放部分权利（Some rights reserved）。

ex.q: Janice finds a picture under CC BY-ND for her friend's photo book. What must she do and not do? (Textbook Ch3 Exercise LQ2(c), adapted)
ex.a: BY: she must give credit to the contributor (title, creator, licence). ND: she must not modify/crop/edit the picture; use it unchanged. Commercial or non-commercial use is allowed.
ex.az: 须注明作者；不可修改图片；商业非商业皆可。

cards.en:
As file-sharing websites and software become popular, it is easy to download pirated software (盜版軟件), music and movies by mistake.

Piracy is not only the unauthorised use and reproduction of copyrighted works in physical ways (photocopying, counterfeit goods 冒牌商品). Unauthorised use and redistribution in digital form are also considered Internet piracy.

Examples (Table 3.2):
  • Watching or listening to pirated music or videos on streaming websites.
  • Downloading pirated games from online platforms such as social media sites, file-sharing sites, cloud and P2P sharing software.
  • Buying a cracked version or membership of copyrighted software illegally through online shopping sites.
Real cases: a game company sued console hackers seeking HKD 25,000 per illegal trade; members of China's largest fansub group were arrested for translating and redistributing TV shows and films without authorisation, with nearly 16 million yuan of illegal income (Global Times, 2021).
cards.zh:
文件分享网站和软件普及，很容易误下载盗版软件 pirated software、音乐和电影。

盗版不只是实体形式（影印、冒牌商品 counterfeit goods）。Unauthorised use and redistribution in digital form are also considered Internet piracy（互联网盗版）。

例子：
  • 在串流网站看/听盗版影音。
  • 从社交网站、文件分享网站、云端、P2P 软件下载盗版游戏。
  • 在网购平台买破解版或会员。
真实案例：游戏公司起诉改机黑客，每宗非法交易索偿 HKD 25,000；中国最大字幕组成员未经授权翻译和分发影视作品，非法收入近 1,600 万元而被捕（2021）。

ex.q: Is it piracy to buy a 'lifetime premium membership' of a paid app for $20 from an online shopping site, when the official price is $300/year?
ex.a: Yes. It is buying a cracked version/membership of copyrighted software illegally through an online shopping site, which is unauthorised use in digital form, i.e. Internet piracy.
ex.az: 是，属于从网购平台非法购买破解会员，即互联网盗版。

cards.en:
Internet piracy is illegal. Besides infringing copyright, it brings practical risks to the user:
  • Security risks such as malware infection (惡意程式感染) and data breach: cracked software may contain viruses, trojans or spyware.
  • No technical support is provided by the copyright owners.
  • Cannot install official updates / bug fixes, so the computer may be attacked through unpatched vulnerabilities.
  • Legal risk: civil lawsuit or criminal prosecution.
Checkpoint 3.2 Q2: Patrick buys cracked software at half price. Possible consequences: his computer may be attacked because bug-fix updates cannot be installed; the act violates IP rights; the software may contain viruses. NOT a consequence: the copyright owner offering him a customised free trial.

Exam wording: 'Pirated software may contain malware, cannot receive security updates or technical support, and using it is copyright infringement.'
cards.zh:
互联网盗版是违法的。除了侵权，对用户还有实际风险：
  • 保安风险：malware infection（恶意程式感染）及data breach（数据外泄），破解软件可能含病毒、木马、间谍软件。
  • 版权持有人不提供技术支援。
  • 不能安装官方更新/修补，漏洞未修补容易被攻击。
  • 法律风险：民事诉讼或刑事检控。
Checkpoint 3.2 Q2：Patrick 半价买破解软件，不可能的后果是“版权持有人为他提供专属免费试用”。

答题句式：Pirated software may contain malware, cannot receive security updates or technical support, and using it is copyright infringement.

ex.q: Janice's sister tells her not to install a 'trial version' of commercial software that a blogger uploaded to his cloud storage. Give TWO reasons. (Textbook Ch3 Exercise LQ2(a))
ex.a:
1. The file may be modified/pirated and contain malware (virus), risking data breach.
2. Downloading/using an unauthorised copy may infringe copyright; it is not from the official source so there is no technical support or updates.
ex.az: 可能含恶意软件；非官方来源，可能侵权且无更新支援。

cards.en:
Copyright infringement affects three groups (Table 3.3):
GroupImpact
CreatorsIf creativity is not well-protected, creators will have no income or motivation to continue creating new and high-quality designs.
PiratesWill be punished, even expelled from the group (school/company); their reputation will be damaged.
CountryWill have a declining reputation and difficulties in the global market.
Answer technique: when a question says 'social impact', name the stakeholder and the effect, e.g. 'Creators lose income, so they lose motivation to create new high-quality works, reducing innovation in society.'
cards.zh:
侵权对三类人有社会影响：
  • 创作者 Creators：创意得不到保护，没有收入和动力继续创作高质素作品。
  • 盗版者 Pirates：会被惩罚，甚至被所属团体开除，声誉受损。
  • 国家 Country：声誉下降，在国际市场上遇到困难。
答题技巧：写“社会影响”时，点名持份者再写后果，例如 Creators lose income, so they lose motivation to create new high-quality works.

ex.q: A university finds a student sharing pirated design software in the student union. State one social impact on the student and one on creators.
ex.a:
Student (pirate): may be punished or expelled; his reputation is damaged.
Creators: lose income from licence sales, so they have less motivation to keep developing high-quality software.
ex.az: 学生：受罚/开除、声誉受损；创作者：失去收入和动力。

cards.en:
Fig 3.3 shows a chain of economic consequences:
  1. Decrease in sales of copyrighted goods (people use pirated copies instead of buying).
  2. No more investors and sponsors (the business is not profitable).
  3. Business closure leads to higher unemployment rate.
  4. The country's tax revenue falls.
In long questions, show the cause-and-effect link rather than listing words: 'Piracy reduces sales of legal copies, so companies earn less and investors withdraw; some companies close, increasing unemployment, and the government collects less tax.'
cards.zh:
图 3.3 是一条经济后果连锁：
  1. 版权产品销量下降 decrease in sales。
  2. 没有投资者和赞助商。
  3. 企业倒闭，失业率上升。
  4. 国家税收下降。
长题要写出因果关系：Piracy reduces sales of legal copies, so companies earn less and investors withdraw; some companies close, increasing unemployment, and the government collects less tax.

ex.q: Explain how widespread game piracy in a city could affect its economy (3 marks).
ex.a: Sales of legitimate games fall → game companies earn less and lose investors/sponsors → some studios close, raising unemployment → government tax revenue falls.
ex.az: 销量下降→失去投资→倒闭失业→税收下降。

cards.en:
To maintain a balance between the interests of the copyright holders and society, the Hong Kong government has implemented IP laws to protect creativity.

Under the Copyright Ordinance, distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences (刑事罪行). The maximum penalty upon selling pirated copy is a fine of $50,000 per pirated copy and imprisonment for 4 years.

Examples of criminal offences (Fig 3.4):
  • Selling infringing copies of films online.
  • Importing and exporting pirated software.
  • Live streaming copyrighted songs without permission.
  • Designing graphics for work with pirated software.
Non-commercial distribution of pirated copies is also a crime if it harms the interest of the copyright owners.
cards.zh:
为了 maintain a balance between the interests of the copyright holders and society，香港政府订立知识产权法例。

根据《版权条例》，distributing and using pirated media and software for commercial purposes are criminal offences（刑事罪行）。出售盗版的最高刑罚：每件盗版罚款 $50,000 及监禁 4 年。

刑事罪行例子：
  • 网上出售侵权电影拷贝。
  • 进出口盗版软件。
  • 未经许可直播版权歌曲。
  • 在工作中用盗版软件设计图像。
非商业分发盗版，如损害版权持有人利益，也属犯罪。

ex.q: A shop owner sells 3 pirated game discs. What is the maximum penalty?
ex.a: Maximum fine $50,000 per pirated copy: 3 × $50,000 = $150,000, plus up to 4 years' imprisonment.

cards.t: Civil lawsuit and the BT case
cards.tz: 民事诉讼与 BT 案
cards.en:
Besides criminal prosecution, copyright owners have the right to ask the buyers or users for monetary compensation through a civil lawsuit (民事訴訟).

Criminal offenceCivil case
Prosecuted by the government (Customs); distributing/using pirated media and software for commercial purposes; up to $50,000 per copy + 4 years' jailStarted by the copyright owner; asks buyers or users for monetary compensation
Hong Kong BitTorrent (BT) case, also known as the Big Crook case (古惑天皇案): a BT user was sentenced to 3 months in prison for distributing copyrighted films using BT technology. This shows that P2P sharing, even without selling, can be a crime when it harms copyright owners.

Checkpoint 3.2 Q1: sharing a commercial Chinese input software with friends via cloud drive: you may be sued for copyright infringement through a civil lawsuit.
cards.zh:
除刑事检控外，版权拥有者有权透过民事诉讼 civil lawsuit 向买家或用户索取金钱赔偿。

分别：刑事罪行由政府（海关）检控，可罚款及监禁；民事诉讼由版权拥有者提出，索取金钱赔偿。

香港 BT 案（古惑天皇案）：一名 BT 用户因 using BT technology to distribute copyrighted films 被判监禁 3 个月。说明 P2P 分享即使没有出售，损害版权持有人利益也可构成刑事罪行。

Checkpoint 3.2 Q1：用云端硬碟把商业中文输入法分享给朋友，可能被版权持有人以民事诉讼控告侵权。

ex.q: Distinguish who starts the action and what outcome is sought in a criminal case vs a civil lawsuit for copyright infringement.
ex.a:
Criminal: the government (Customs and Excise Department) prosecutes; outcome is punishment (fine, imprisonment).
Civil: the copyright owner sues; outcome is monetary compensation from the infringer.
ex.az: 刑事：政府检控求惩罚；民事：版权拥有者起诉求赔偿。

cards.t: IP authorities: IPD vs Customs and Excise
cards.tz: 知识产权署 vs 香港海关
cards.en:
Two Hong Kong authorities protect IP in different aspects (Table 3.4):
AuthorityRole and functions
Intellectual Property Department (IPD, 知識產權署)Advising on policies and legislation to protect IPR; registration of trademarks, patents, designs and copyright licensing bodies; promotion and education of IP
Customs and Excise Department (C&ED, 香港海關)Protecting the interests of IPR owners and legitimate users by taking criminal sanctions (刑事制裁) against copyright and trademark infringements
Example 3.1: selling cracked apps on online shopping platforms → your action may be considered a criminal offence. Even if the copyright owner does not complain, C&ED can still take legal action. ONLY the Customs and Excise Department takes criminal sanctions; not the IPD, not the OGCIO.

Real case: in 2018 HK Customs acted against the sale of pirated game consoles on social media, preloaded with over 5,000 pirated games.
cards.zh:
香港两个部门分工保护知识产权：
  • 知识产权署 Intellectual Property Department：就保护知识产权的政策及法例提供意见；注册商标、专利、外观设计及版权授权团体；推广及教育。
  • 香港海关 Customs and Excise Department：taking criminal sanctions（刑事制裁）against copyright and trademark infringements，保护权利人和合法用户。
Example 3.1：在网购平台卖破解 app → 可能构成刑事罪行。即使版权持有人不投诉，海关仍可采取行动。只有海关负责刑事制裁，知识产权署和 OGCIO 不是。

2018 年海关打击社交平台出售预载逾 5,000 款盗版游戏的游戏机。

ex.q: A tutor photocopies a whole book and distributes copies to students. To whom can the copyright holders complain about the pirated copies? (Textbook Ch3 Checkpoint 3.4 Q2)
ex.a: The Customs and Excise Department, because it takes criminal sanctions against copyright infringement. (Not the IPD, which handles policy, registration and education; registering copyright is unnecessary; this is not fair dealing.)
ex.az: 向香港海关投诉。

cards.en:
The Copyright Ordinance protects not only the copyright owners but also the users. There are exceptions to copyright that allow limited use of a copyrighted work without the permission of the copyright owner.

Fair dealing (公平處理) of copyrighted material is allowed for certain purposes, including but not limited to (Table 3.5):
PurposeExamples
EducationComparing characteristics of modern and classical music; discussing applications of new technology
Non-commercial research and private studyDiscussing the ideology behind Cantonese pop songs of the 1980s; discussing features of texting language
Criticism, review and news reportingEvaluating the features and quality of a product; criticising bad acting in a TV drama
Key idea: fair dealing is about limited use for a permitted purpose, normally non-profit, that does not replace the market for the original.
cards.zh:
《版权条例》不只保护版权拥有者，也保护用户。有一些 exceptions to copyright that allow limited use of a copyrighted work without the permission of the copyright owner。

公平处理 Fair dealing 适用于以下目的（不限于）：
  • 教育 Education：比较现代与古典音乐、讨论新科技应用。
  • 非商业研究及私人研习 Non-commercial research and private study：讨论 80 年代广东流行曲背后的思想、讨论短讯语言特色。
  • 批评、评论及新闻报道 Criticism, review and news reporting：评估产品功能质素、批评电视剧演技。
重点：公平处理是为许可目的作有限度、一般非牟利的使用，不会取代原作的市场。

ex.q: A YouTuber shows a 10-second clip of a phone advert while reviewing the phone's camera quality. Which fair-dealing purpose may apply?
ex.a: Criticism, review and news reporting: the clip is used in a limited way to evaluate the features and quality of a product.
ex.az: 批评、评论及新闻报道。

cards.t: Fair dealing or infringement? School cases
cards.tz: 公平处理还是侵权？学校个案
cards.en:
Not all acts for educational purposes can be exempted. Fig 3.5:
Not fair dealing (infringement)Fair dealing
Downloading and distributing the whole e-textbook to studentsShowing parts of movies or TV programmes for the purpose of instruction
Using copyrighted software for a school assignment without a proper licenceAttaching copyrighted images to the assignment
Copying copyrighted software code and claiming it as your own workPrinting a piece of a journal article for personal study
Tests to apply: How much is used (part vs whole)? Is it commercial? Does it replace buying the original? Is it relevant to the learning objective? (Only fair, non-profit educational use is exempted; distributing works irrelevant to the course may be illegal.)

Checkpoint 3.3 Q2: most likely fair dealing = playing a few minutes of a documentary in a lesson to illustrate a historical event; not copying a whole article, showing a whole film, or distributing HKDSE past papers free.
cards.zh:
不是所有教育用途都可豁免。图 3.5：
  • 不公平（侵权）：下载并向学生派发整本电子课本；功课使用没有正当授权的软件；复制别人代码并声称是自己的作品。
  • 公平处理：教学时播放电影/电视节目的部分片段；在功课中附上版权图片；为私人研习打印期刊文章的一部分。
判断准则：用了多少（部分/全部）？是否商业？会否取代购买原作？是否与教学目标相关？（只有公平、非牟利的教育用途获豁免。）

Checkpoint 3.3 Q2：最可能属公平处理是上课播放几分钟纪录片说明历史事件。

ex.q: Which is fair dealing? A. Copy an entire web article into an assignment B. Show an entire film in English class C. Play a few minutes of a documentary to illustrate history D. Distribute HKDSE past papers free (Textbook Ch3 Checkpoint 3.3 Q2)
ex.a: C. Only a small part is used, for instruction, non-commercially. A, B and D use whole works, which replaces the original and is not fair dealing.
ex.az: 答案 C：只用一小部分作教学。

cards.t: When the dealing is unfair: news cases
cards.tz: 不公平处理的新闻个案
cards.en:
Activity 3.3 asks why these acts are not fair dealing:
  • Selling pirated HKDSE teaching notes (HK Customs, 2020): a copyright holder complained and Customs took action against sales on multiple online platforms; copies were emailed to buyers after electronic payment. Not fair dealing because it is commercial (selling for profit) and copies the whole work, replacing the market for the real notes. The educational subject does not make it education use.
  • 'Fast movies' in Japan (2021): three people arrested for posting illegally edited short versions of films that explain the entire plot, sharing advertising revenue. Not fair dealing because it reveals the whole story (substitutes for watching the film) and earns profit; it is not genuine criticism or review.
Checkpoint 3.3 Q1: Peter's public-housing photos. Illegal: a publisher putting them in a textbook (commercial use) and a friend reposting them on social media without permission. Legal: a teacher illustrating old estates with one photo in a lesson; a friend printing a photo with permission.
cards.zh:
Activity 3.3：为何以下不是公平处理？
  • 出售盗版 HKDSE 教学笔记（海关 2020）：版权持有人投诉，海关打击多个网上平台的销售，买家电子付款后收电邮副本。因为是商业牟利并复制整份作品，取代正版市场；题材是教育不等于属教育用途。
  • 日本“快速电影 fast movies”（2021）：三人上载剪辑版电影、讲解整个剧情，并分享广告收入而被捕。因披露全部剧情、取代观看原片，又有利润，并非真正评论。
Checkpoint 3.3 Q1：Peter 的屋邨照片——出版社放进课本（商业）、朋友未经许可转发：违法；老师上课用一张照片说明、朋友经许可打印：合法。答案 (1) 和 (3)。

ex.q: A student uploads a 10-minute video summarising an entire new movie scene by scene and earns ad revenue. Is it fair dealing? Explain.
ex.a: No. It reproduces/reveals essentially the whole work so viewers may not need to watch the original, and it is for profit (ad revenue). Fair dealing only allows limited use for purposes like genuine criticism/review, non-commercially.
ex.az: 不是：等同整部作品并有广告收入。

cards.en:
Besides legislation, the Intellectual Property Department promotes the importance of IP to the public. Both the users and copyright holders have a responsibility to protect IPR to foster innovation.

Users should obtain permission from the copyright holders, and to avoid unintentional infringement, read the terms and conditions before using the copyrighted material.

Four basic steps to avoid copyright infringement as a user (Fig 3.6):
  1. Identify the copyright owners.
  2. Obtain permissions or licences.
  3. Use the work according to the terms of use.
  4. Acknowledge the source properly.
Checkpoint 3.4 Q3: John wants to use a copyrighted song in his vlog → identify the owner, obtain permission/licence (or choose royalty-free / CC-licensed music), follow the licence terms, and credit the song.
cards.zh:
除了立法，知识产权署也向公众推广知识产权的重要。Both the users and copyright holders have a responsibility to protect IPR to foster innovation.

用户应取得版权持有人许可，并在使用前阅读条款及细则，避免无意侵权。

用户避免侵权四步（图 3.6）：
  1. Identify 找出版权拥有者。
  2. Obtain 取得许可或授权。
  3. Use 按使用条款使用。
  4. Acknowledge 正确注明来源。
Checkpoint 3.4 Q3：John 想在 vlog 用版权歌曲 → 找出拥有者、取得授权（或改用免版税/CC 音乐）、按条款使用、注明出处。

ex.q: A school club wants to play a pop song in its promotional video. Apply the four steps.
ex.a:
1. Identify the copyright owner (record company/composer).
2. Obtain permission or buy a licence.
3. Use the song only within the licence terms (e.g. length, platforms).
4. Acknowledge the song title, artist and licence in the video credits.
ex.az: 找拥有者→取得授权→按条款→注明出处。

cards.tz: 注明出处与 CC 署名
cards.en:
Giving credit to the copyrighted works is important. It acknowledges the copyright owners' effort and helps avoid copyright infringement and plagiarism. For instance, appropriate attribution is required under the CC licence.

Attribution format (Activity 3.4):
"Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0.
  title    creator                licence
It is better to include links to the original photo and the licence where possible.

Remember the order Title – Creator – Licence (often called TCL). Example answer for the activity's second image: "20160314-ZD4_6150" by zhao hui is licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

Note: under CC BY-SA, if you adapt the image you must also share your version under CC BY-SA.
cards.zh:
注明出处很重要：它 acknowledges the copyright owners' effort，并 helps avoid copyright infringement and plagiarism。CC 授权规定必须适当署名。

署名格式（Activity 3.4）："Cat" by Y.Hino is licensed under CC BY 2.0. 依次是标题 title – 作者 creator – 授权 licence。最好附上原图和授权条款的链接。

第二张图的答案："20160314-ZD4_6150" by zhao hui is licensed under CC BY-SA 2.0.

注意：CC BY-SA 下如改编图片，新作品也要用 CC BY-SA 分享。

ex.q: Write an attribution for a photo titled 'Victoria Harbour Night' by Chan Siu Ming under CC BY-NC 4.0.
ex.a: "Victoria Harbour Night" by Chan Siu Ming is licensed under CC BY-NC 4.0. (Add links to the photo and licence if possible; do not use it commercially.)
ex.az: 标题+作者+授权，并不可商业使用。

cards.en:
In academic writing (APA style, Enrichment):
  • In-text citation means citing the author and the year of publication for the source in the body of an article, e.g. Patrick (2008) found that...
  • The reference list is attached at the end of the article to provide further information for readers, e.g. Patrick, D. (2008). Street Food Culture. Hong Kong: ABC Press.
Why it matters: universities treat plagiarism seriously. In 2020 CUHK's Senate Committee on Student Discipline announced that the most extreme penalty for plagiarism, including self-plagiarism, would be expulsion.

APA reference pattern: Surname, Initial. (Year). Title. Place: Publisher.
cards.zh:
学术写作（APA 格式）：
  • 文内引用 In-text citation：在正文中注明作者和出版年份，例如 Patrick (2008) found that...
  • 参考书目 Reference list：附在文章末，为读者提供详细资料，例如 Patrick, D. (2008). Street Food Culture. Hong Kong: ABC Press.
重要性：2020 年中大学生纪律委员会宣布，抄袭（包括自我抄袭 self-plagiarism）最严重可被开除学籍。

APA 格式：姓, 名首字母. (年份). 书名. 地点: 出版社.

ex.q: Format a reference-list entry and an in-text citation for: author Mary Wong, book 'Smart City Data', 2019, published by XYZ Press in Hong Kong.
ex.a:
Reference list: Wong, M. (2019). Smart City Data. Hong Kong: XYZ Press.
In-text: Wong (2019) found that ...
ex.az: 参考书目：Wong, M. (2019)...；文内：Wong (2019)。

cards.tz: 误解：抄袭 vs 侵犯版权
cards.en:
Misconception: 'Plagiarism (抄襲) always involves copyright infringement.' Wrong.

Copyright infringement may occur, but not always, in plagiarism, and vice versa. In general, plagiarism is unethical while copyright infringement is illegal.

Plagiarism means using another person's work without acknowledgement. If you use some copyrighted images in slides to present your idea, it is not considered copyright infringement (fair dealing for education), but it will be considered plagiarism without giving proper credit.
PlagiarismCopyright infringement
NatureUnethical (academic misconduct)Illegal
Key problemNo acknowledgementNo permission / beyond exceptions
FixCite the sourceGet permission / licence
Also: crediting the source does not make an unauthorised copy legal. Selling a whole book with the author's name printed on it is still infringement.
cards.zh:
误解：“抄袭一定涉及侵犯版权。”错。

Copyright infringement may occur, but not always, in plagiarism, and vice versa. In general, plagiarism is unethical while copyright infringement is illegal.

抄袭 Plagiarism = using another person's work without acknowledgement. 在简报中用版权图片说明意念，不算侵权（教育用途的公平处理），但如没有注明出处就是抄袭。

对比：抄袭是不道德，问题在没注明出处，补救是引用来源；侵权是违法，问题在没获许可，补救是取得授权。另外，注明出处不会令未经授权的复制变合法。

ex.q: Classify: (a) Amy copies two paragraphs from a public-domain 19th-century novel into her essay without quotation or citation. (b) Ben sells photocopies of a new textbook, crediting the author on the cover.
ex.a:
(a) Plagiarism but not copyright infringement (the work is in the public domain; the problem is no acknowledgement).
(b) Copyright infringement but not plagiarism (he credited the author, but copied and sold without permission).
ex.az: (a)抄袭非侵权 (b)侵权非抄袭。

cards.tz: 版权持有人保护版权的方法
cards.en:
Copyright holders have a responsibility to set terms and conditions to limit the use of granted copyright, such as publishing work with a CC licence. It is also important to read the agreement if it is set by other parties. For instance, a social media site may obtain the right to reuse your uploaded content under their terms of use.

Four basic steps to protect copyright as a copyright holder (Fig 3.7):
  1. State the copyright in your work (not legally necessary).
  2. Register corresponding IP such as patent.
  3. Set the terms of use of the granted copyright.
  4. Grant copyright for others to use your work.
Copyright notices (Enrichment): not legally required but good practice to alert readers, e.g. 2016 © Intellectual Property Department. Other notices: © All rights reserved; Some rights reserved (CC); Pixabay License (free for commercial use, no attribution required).
cards.zh:
版权持有人有责任设定条款，限制所授出版权的使用，例如以 CC 授权发布。若条款由别人订立，也要细阅协议，例如社交平台可能按其使用条款取得重用你上载内容的权利。

持有人保护版权四步（图 3.7）：
  1. State 在作品中声明版权（法律上非必要）。
  2. Register 注册相应知识产权，如专利。
  3. Set 订立使用条款。
  4. Grant 授权他人使用。
版权声明：非法律规定但属好习惯，如 2016 © Intellectual Property Department；其他：© All rights reserved、Some rights reserved（CC）、Pixabay License（可商用，毋须署名）。

ex.q: Amy posts a vlog without a © notice. Can news media repost her entire vlog without permission? (Textbook Ch3 Exercise LQ4(b))
ex.a: No. Copyright is given automatically when the work is created; a © notice is not legally required. Reposting the entire vlog is not limited fair dealing for news reporting, so the media needs her permission.
ex.az: 不可以：版权自动产生，整段转载需许可。

cards.en:
Some programs are free while some have a price. Copyright also protects elements of software such as source code and interface design.

Different types of licences (特許使用權) are granted to the users by the developers to define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages. If the users do not follow the terms of use, it may lead to copyright infringement.

Generally, software can be classified into 4 types: commercial software, shareware, freeware and open source software.

Important: buying software means buying a licence to use it, not the copyright. E.g. an 'educational use' licence obtained free by a student does not allow commercial use: Checkpoint 3.5 Q2: Patrick, who installed video editing software free for educational use, must read the licence agreement to check if it can be used for commercial purposes before using it for a freelance job.
cards.zh:
有些程序免费，有些要付钱。Copyright also protects elements of software such as source code and interface design.

开发者向用户授出不同的特许使用权 licences，define how the software can be used or the restriction of certain usages。不遵守使用条款可能构成侵权。

软件一般分 4 类：commercial software、shareware、freeware、open source software。

注意：买软件是买使用授权，不是买版权。例如学生免费取得的“教育用途”授权不容许商业用途。Checkpoint 3.5 Q2：Patrick 接自由职业剪片前，应阅读授权协议，确认能否作商业用途。

ex.q: A student gets Photoshop through a school education licence and wants to design paid posters for a shop. What should she check and why?
ex.a: She should read the licence agreement to check whether commercial use is permitted. Educational licences are often restricted to non-commercial use; using it for paid work would break the terms of use and may be copyright infringement.
ex.az: 阅读授权条款看是否容许商业用途。

cards.t: Four types of software licence compared
cards.en:
CommercialSharewareFreewareOpen source
PriceLicence fee; sometimes free/cheaper for educationFree time-limited or feature-limited trial; ads may be shownFreeFree
Multiple usersSingle-user / multi-user / site licenceUsually similar to commercialUnlimitedUnlimited
Source code accessNoNoNoYes: free to use, modify, copy, distribute
CopyingNoNoYesYes
RedistributionNoNoYesYes
Commercial useIncluded in licence feeIncluded in licence feeUsually free; may be restricted to non-commercial, private useFree
Technical supportYesYesLimited / noneLimited / none
ExamplesMicrosoft Office, Adobe PhotoshopWinZip, Lightworks, PhotopeaBrowsers (Edge, Chrome), IM (WhatsApp, Signal)Linux, Firefox, OpenOffice, GIMP, Android
Tip: shareware is very common on mobile platforms. The key difference between freeware and open source: only open source gives access to the source code.
cards.zh:
四类软件比较（要背）：
  • 商用软件 Commercial：收牌照费（教育版有时免费/较平）；单用户/多用户/场地授权；不可看源码、不可复制或再分发；商业用途已含在费用中；有技术支援。例：Microsoft Office、Adobe Photoshop。
  • 共享软件 Shareware：免费试用（限时或限功能），或显示广告赚钱；其余与商用相似。例：WinZip、Lightworks、Photopea。手机上很常见。
  • 免费软件 Freeware：免费、用户数无限；可复制、可再分发；不可看源码；商用通常免费，但可能只限非商业私人用途；支援有限或没有。例：Edge、Chrome、WhatsApp、Signal。
  • 开放源码软件 Open source：免费、无限；可看、改、复制、分发源码；商用免费；支援有限。例：Linux、Firefox、OpenOffice、GIMP、Android。

ex.q: Lily finds Software P (free, she may edit the code) and Software Q (free for 30 days). Which is shareware? Which is open source? (Textbook Ch3 Exercise LQ1(a))
ex.a: Q is shareware (free only for a time-limited trial). P is open source software (free and the source code can be modified).
ex.az: Q 是共享软件，P 是开放源码软件。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a user
cards.tz: 用户角度：选择软件类型
cards.en:
Example 3.2: What should I choose as a user?
ProsCons
CommercialFrequent updates and technical support; usually ads-freeHigher cost; cannot modify the code
SharewareFree for basic feature; free trial before purchasing; frequent updates and technical supportCannot modify the code; cost for full version or premium feature; ads may show
FreewareFree to use; can copy and redistribute the software freelyCannot modify the code; less technical support; may be restricted to personal use
Open sourceFree to use; free to view and modify the source code; free to publish the modified version; simplifies licence purchase procedureLess technical support
Checkpoint 3.5 Q1: disadvantages of shareware for George: advanced features may be available only when you purchase and it is only free for the trial period. (Source code being modified by others is not an issue, and shareware usually does have support.)
cards.zh:
Example 3.2：作为用户怎么选？
  • 商用：优点：经常更新、有技术支援、通常无广告；缺点：成本高、不能改源码。
  • 共享：优点：基本功能免费、可先试用、有更新和支援；缺点：不能改码、完整版/高级功能要付钱、可能有广告。
  • 免费：优点：免费、可自由复制及再分发；缺点：不能改码、支援少、可能只限个人用途。
  • 开源：优点：免费、可看及修改源码、可发布修改版、简化购买授权手续；缺点：技术支援少。
Checkpoint 3.5 Q1：共享软件的缺点是高级功能要购买及只在试用期免费，答案 B。

ex.q: David wants video editing software for his vlogs. Give one pro and one con each for commercial and open source software. (Textbook Ch3 Exercise LQ3)
ex.a:
Commercial: Pro: frequent updates and technical support / ads-free. Con: higher cost; cannot modify code.
Open source: Pro: free; can view and modify source code. Con: less technical support.
ex.az: 商用：有支援/成本高；开源：免费可改码/支援少。

cards.t: Choosing a licence type as a developer
cards.tz: 开发者角度：选择授权模式
cards.en:
Example 3.2: What should I choose as a developer?
ProsCons
CommercialEarn money for each purchase or subscription; users are prohibited to copy and redistribute the softwareFewer people can use the software
SharewareEarn money from the ads; promote and persuade users to purchase the software during trial periodNo income if users block the ads or do not pay for feature upgrade
FreewareProhibit users from modifying the code; allow users to use and redistribute; more people can use itNo income from licence fee
Open sourceUsers can study and modify the code; cooperate with users to develop the software; more people can use itNo income from licence fee
Textbook Exercise MC10 (reasons to publish as shareware): make money for authorising use, not give up copyright, attract more people to try it. Wanting others to improve the source code together is a reason for open source, not shareware.
cards.zh:
Example 3.2：作为开发者怎么选？
  • 商用：每次购买/订阅都有收入，禁止用户复制分发；缺点：用户较少。
  • 共享：靠广告赚钱，试用期间推广说服用户购买；缺点：用户屏蔽广告或不升级就没收入。
  • 免费：禁止用户改码，容许使用和再分发，用户多；缺点：没有牌照费收入。
  • 开源：用户可研究和修改代码，与用户合作开发，用户多；缺点：没有牌照费收入。
课本 MC10：发布为共享软件的原因是赚钱、保留版权、吸引更多人试用；“想大家一起改进源码”是开源的理由。

ex.q: An indie developer wants as many people as possible to use her game but does not want anyone to change her code, and does not need income. Which licence suits her?
ex.a: Freeware: it is free with unlimited users and can be redistributed (more people use it), but the source code is not released, so users cannot modify it.
ex.az: 免费软件。

cards.t: Misconception: freeware and open source are not uncopyrighted
cards.tz: 误解：免费及开源软件也有版权
cards.en:
Misconception: 'Freeware and open source software are uncopyrighted.' Wrong.

Only public domain software is uncopyrighted. Freeware, shareware, open source software and commercial software only grant users rights to use the software under different licence agreements. The developer still owns the copyright.

Consequences:
  • Breaking the open source licence terms (e.g. not keeping the licence notice) can still be infringement.
  • If Lily modifies most of open source Software P and redistributes it, the original author keeps copyright of the original code, and Lily owns copyright only in her own new contributions; she must follow the open source licence. (Exercise LQ1(b))
  • Freeware being 'free' does not let you sell it or modify it.
Similarity vs difference (Checkpoint 3.5 Q3): both freeware and open source are free to use, copy and redistribute; but only open source allows access to and modification of the source code.
cards.zh:
误解：“免费软件和开源软件没有版权。”错。

Only public domain software is uncopyrighted. 免费、共享、开源及商用软件都只是按不同授权协议给予用户使用权，开发者仍拥有版权。

后果：
  • 违反开源授权条款（如没保留授权声明）仍可能侵权。
  • Lily 大幅修改开源软件 P 再分发：原作者仍拥有原代码版权，Lily 只拥有自己新增部分，并须遵守开源授权（课本 LQ1(b)）。
  • 免费软件不代表可以出售或修改。
相同与不同（Checkpoint 3.5 Q3）：两者都免费、可复制及再分发；只有开源可取得及修改源码。

ex.q: State one similarity and one difference between freeware and open source software. (Textbook Ch3 Checkpoint 3.5 Q3)
ex.a:
Similarity: both are free to use and can be copied/redistributed (unlimited users).
Difference: open source software lets users access and modify the source code; freeware does not.
ex.az: 相同：免费可分发；不同：只有开源可看改源码。

cards.t: User licence: single-user, multi-user and site licence
cards.tz: 用户授权：单用户、多用户、场地授权
cards.en:
The commercial and shareware licensing scheme usually indicates the number of authorised users for each licence. Read the licence agreement and buy the respective licence to avoid unintentional infringement.
  • Single-user licence (單用戶特許使用權): the software can be installed on only one device or only one user can use the software at a time.
  • Multi-user licence / Site licence (多用戶 / 場地特許使用權): unlimited or a defined number of users from a company, an organisation or an institute are granted the right to use the software. A site licence may limit the use of the software at a particular location.
Tip: a family subscription plan allows a defined number of users who live together to use premium functions at a time.

Exercise LQ5: a university department buys a single-user licence and installs it on all office computers. This violates the Copyright Ordinance because the licence allows only one device/user; they make unauthorised copies. Fix: buy a multi-user or site licence (or enough single-user licences).
cards.zh:
商用及共享软件的授权通常注明每个授权的认可用户数目，应阅读协议并购买合适授权。
  • 单用户授权 Single-user licence：only one device or only one user at a time。
  • 多用户/场地授权 Multi-user / Site licence：公司、机构或学院的无限或指定数目用户可使用；场地授权可能只限在特定地点使用。
提示：家庭订阅计划容许同住的指定人数同时使用高级功能。

课本 LQ5：大学部门买单用户授权却装在所有办公室电脑 → 违反授权，属未经授权复制。应购买多用户或场地授权（或足够数量的单用户授权）。

ex.q: A school with 40 computer-room PCs buys one single-user licence of a program and activates it on all PCs. Explain the problem and the solution. (cf. Textbook Ch3 Exercise MC11(3))
ex.a: A single-user licence allows installation on only one device / one user at a time, so 39 installations are unauthorised copies, i.e. copyright infringement. The school should buy a site licence (for the school premises) or a multi-user licence covering 40 users.
ex.az: 只容许一部机；应买场地或多用户授权。

cards.en:
Unlike the traditional one-off licence fee, more and more software companies have switched to a subscription model that treats software as a service and requires users to pay for the licence monthly or annually.

SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing (雲端運算).

Fig 3.9: the provider hosts the servers, database, code, application and help desk in the cloud; business users, institutional users and personal users access the SaaS over an Internet connection.

Examples: Microsoft 365, Adobe Creative Cloud, Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Spotify, Netflix.

Implications: users do not manage installation or servers; updates are applied centrally; but they depend on the Internet and stop having access when the subscription ends.
cards.zh:
与传统一次性牌照费不同，越来越多软件公司改用订阅模式，把软件当作服务，用户按月或按年付费。

SaaS is also known as web-based software because it is centrally hosted by the software company based on cloud computing.

图 3.9：供应商在云端托管伺服器、数据库、代码、应用程式和服务台；商业、机构及个人用户经互联网使用。

例子：Microsoft 365、Adobe Creative Cloud、Zoom、Teams、Spotify、Netflix。

影响：用户毋须自行安装和管理伺服器，更新由供应商统一处理；但依赖网络，停止订阅便不能使用。

ex.q: Why is SaaS also called web-based software?
ex.a: Because the software is centrally hosted by the software company on cloud computing servers, and users access it through the Internet (e.g. a web browser or thin app) instead of installing and running everything locally.
ex.az: 因为由软件公司在云端集中托管，用户经互联网使用。

cards.tz: 永久授权 vs 订阅
cards.en:
Perpetual licence (永久性授權)Subscription (訂閱)
ProsIndefinite use with one-off payment; Internet connection not required; faster response time; better security control without data transmission on the cloudA trial period is usually provided; backup service on cloud; simpler installation (hosted on cloud); access on multiple devices by account login; free frequent updates and ongoing technical support
ConsAdditional costs may be charged for maintenance and software updates; usually limited and linked to a certain number of devicesInternet connection may be required; response time may be longer in order to connect to the server
ExamplesMicrosoft Office Home and Student 2019; Adobe Creative Suite 6Netflix, ViuTV, Amazon, Spotify, KKBOX; Teams, Zoom, Skype; Adobe Creative Cloud; Microsoft 365
Choosing: a user with unstable Internet or sensitive data → perpetual; a user with several devices who wants latest features and cloud backup → subscription.
cards.zh:
永久授权 Perpetual licence：优点：一次付款无限期使用；毋须上网；反应较快；数据不经云端传送，保安控制较好。缺点：维护和更新可能另外收费；通常只限指定数目装置。例：Office Home and Student 2019、Adobe Creative Suite 6。

订阅 Subscription：优点：通常有试用期；云端备份；安装简单；登入帐户即可在多部装置使用；免费经常更新及持续支援。缺点：可能需要上网；连接伺服器反应时间较长。例：Netflix、Spotify、KKBOX、Teams、Zoom、Adobe Creative Cloud、Microsoft 365。

选择：网络不稳或数据敏感 → 永久；多装置、要最新功能和备份 → 订阅。

ex.q: A law firm handles confidential files and has unreliable Internet. Should it choose a perpetual licence or a subscription for its document software? Give two reasons.
ex.a: Perpetual licence: (1) it works without an Internet connection; (2) better security control because data need not be transmitted to the cloud (also faster response time).
ex.az: 永久授权：不需上网、数据不上云更安全。

cards.en:
Licence key, activation key or product key is a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software. During the software installation, the user needs to enter the licence key to register or activate the software application (Fig 3.10, e.g. six groups of characters).

Purpose: only paying users can activate, so a copied installer alone is useless; the vendor can track how many times each key is activated.

Hardware key (USB dongle) (Enrichment): a physical device plugged into the USB port that is used for unlocking the software; it can also be used for two-factor authentication.

Summary table: Licence key: feature = a string of characters given to an authorised user who paid; application = device-locked licence (installation on a single device) and user-locked licence (one user at a time).
cards.zh:
Licence key / activation key / product key（序号、启用码） 是 a string of characters given to an authorised user who has paid for the software。安装时用户须输入序号以注册或启用软件（图 3.10）。

目的：只有付费用户能启用，单单复制安装档没用；厂商也可追踪每个序号启用了多少次。

硬件钥匙 USB dongle（增润）：插入 USB 端口来解锁软件，也可用于双重认证 two-factor authentication。

总结：序号的应用包括 device-locked licence（只装一部机）和 user-locked licence（同一时间一个用户）。

ex.q: Why does a licence key help reduce piracy compared with just selling a downloadable installer?
ex.a: The installer can be copied freely, but the software will not run without a valid key that is only given to paying users. The vendor can also limit the number of activations per key, so sharing one key among many people fails.
ex.az: 没有付费取得的有效序号便无法启用，且可限制启用次数。

cards.tz: 锁定装置 vs 锁定用户授权
cards.en:
Device-locked licence: only allows installation on a single device. The licence key is locked to the unique machine ID of your device during software installation (machine ID = a unique code given to identify a specific device). Some companies allow more than one device (e.g. a desktop and a laptop), but still only one user at a time. If you exceed the maximum number of activations, an error such as 'Invalid licence key' may pop up (Fig 3.11).

User-locked licence: usually requires registration for activation. Users must agree to the terms and conditions (checking a box or just signing up). The licence key is locked to a specific account. Users can use the software on any devices but they need to remain signed in to activate it. Usually only one user at a time for a single-user licence. User-locked licensing is an example of a floating licence that allows installation on multiple devices.
Device-lockedUser-locked
Locked toMachine IDUser account
DevicesOne (or a few)Any, while signed in
cards.zh:
锁定装置授权 Device-locked licence：只容许安装在一部装置；安装时序号与装置独有的 machine ID 绑定（machine ID = 识别某部装置的独有编码）。有些公司容许两部机（如桌面和手提），但同一时间仍只一个用户。超过最多启用次数会出现 Invalid licence key。

锁定用户授权 User-locked licence：通常需要注册才可启用，用户须同意条款（剔选方格或注册）；序号与帐户绑定；可在任何装置使用，但须保持登入；单用户授权通常同一时间只限一人。它是浮动授权 floating licence 的例子，可装在多部装置。

ex.q: Kelly reinstalls a device-locked program on her new laptop with the same key and gets 'Invalid licence key'. Explain why.
ex.a: The key was locked to the machine ID of her old computer, and the maximum number of activations for the key has been reached, so activation on a new machine ID is rejected (she may need to deactivate the old device or contact the vendor).
ex.az: 序号绑定旧机 machine ID，已超出启用次数。

cards.en:
Digital watermark technology is embedding data into a digital work such as images, videos, texts or other digital content.
  • Visible watermark: a mark put inside the carrying object and made clear to the user (e.g. 'Watermark' text across a photo).
  • Invisible watermark: a mark embedded in the carrying object but cannot be seen, and can be extracted using watermarking algorithms.
Why invisible watermarks are popular: they are harder to remove, do not affect the carrying object, and remain unchanged and can be extracted even after being modified by pirates through cropping, resizing and compression.

Fig 3.15 process:
  • Insertion: original data + invisible watermark (bits such as 0101 1100 0110) → watermarked data.
  • Extraction: watermarked data with modification (cropped, resized, compressed, edited) → embedded watermark remains unchanged.
Note: a visible watermark can simply be cropped or edited out; removing a watermark from a copyrighted photo and uploading it is infringement.
cards.zh:
数码水印 Digital watermark：embedding data into a digital work such as images, videos, texts or other digital content。
  • 可见水印 Visible：放在载体内，用户清楚看见。
  • 隐形水印 Invisible：嵌入载体但看不见，可用水印算法提取。
隐形水印的好处：较难移除、不影响载体、即使盗版者裁剪、缩放、压缩，水印仍不变并可提取。

图 3.15：插入：原数据 + 隐形水印 → 已加水印数据；提取：被修改过的数据 → 嵌入的水印保持不变。

注意：可见水印可被裁走；移除版权照片的水印再上载属侵权。

ex.q: A photographer sells photos online. Give two reasons to use an invisible rather than a visible watermark.
ex.a:
1. It does not affect the appearance/quality of the photo for paying customers.
2. It is harder to remove and survives cropping, resizing and compression, so ownership can still be extracted and proved from pirated copies.
ex.az: 不影响相片；难移除，裁剪压缩后仍可提取。

cards.en:
Table 3.8 Applications of digital watermark:
ApplicationMethod
Digital copyright protectionThe ownership rights are embedded to prove copyright infringement.
Source tracingData given to different recipients is watermarked differently. This is useful to trace the person who leaks the confidential information.
Real case (Beijing News, 2016): Alibaba fired employees who hacked the internal sales system to get more mooncakes than allowed. Alibaba traced back to the employee who leaked the screenshot of this internal news using digital watermark: each employee's view of the internal page carried a different hidden mark.

Exercise MC8: digital watermark can help prevent unauthorised distribution of digital images; a digital signature verifies the sender, and SSL encrypts data in transmission, so they do not stop image redistribution. Checkpoint 3.6: for videos on streaming sites, the answer is digital watermarks only.
cards.zh:
表 3.8 数码水印应用：
  • 数码版权保护 Digital copyright protection：The ownership rights are embedded to prove copyright infringement.
  • 来源追踪 Source tracing：Data given to different recipients is watermarked differently，用来追查泄露机密资料的人。
真实个案（2016）：阿里巴巴员工入侵内部系统多抢月饼被解雇；公司用数码水印追查到泄露内部消息截图的员工，因每名员工看到的页面带不同隐藏标记。

课本 MC8：防止数码图像被未经授权分发的是数码水印；数码签署验证发送者，SSL 加密传输，都不能阻止转发。Checkpoint 3.6：串流网站影片的保护答案是只有数码水印。

ex.q: A company sends the same confidential PDF to 5 partners and a copy leaks online. How can digital watermarking identify the leaker?
ex.a: Before sending, embed a different invisible watermark (e.g. a partner ID) into each partner's copy. Extract the watermark from the leaked copy with the watermarking algorithm; since it survives cropping/compression, the ID shows which partner's copy was leaked.
ex.az: 每份嵌入不同隐形水印，从外泄副本提取即可识别。

cards.en:
Digital signature is a technology used for verifying the sender's identity. It is commonly applied in detecting the unauthorised modification and forgery (贗品) such as pirated software.

How it protects IP: the legitimate software company digitally signs its program files. If a pirate modifies the program (e.g. cracks it or adds malware), the signature no longer matches, so the user can tell the file is not the genuine, unmodified product.

Activity 3.5: check the signer on Windows:
  1. Right-click the application file.
  2. Click Properties.
  3. Open the Digital Signatures tab to see the name of the signer (e.g. Adobe Systems), the digest algorithm (e.g. sha1) and the timestamp.
Compare: a digital watermark proves ownership / traces source of content; a digital signature verifies who sent it and that it was not modified.
cards.zh:
数码签署 Digital signature 是 a technology used for verifying the sender's identity，常用于 detecting the unauthorised modification and forgery（赝品）such as pirated software。

原理：正版软件公司为程序档案加上数码签署。若盗版者修改程序（破解或加入恶意程式），签署便不吻合，用户可知档案并非原装未改的正版。

Activity 3.5（Windows 查看签署者）：右键点应用程式 → Properties → Digital Signatures 分页，可见签署者名称（如 Adobe Systems）、摘要算法（如 sha1）和时间戳。

比较：数码水印证明拥有权/追查来源；数码签署验证发送者及内容未被修改。

ex.q: You download an installer claiming to be from Adobe. How can you check it is genuine and unmodified?
ex.a: Right-click the file → Properties → Digital Signatures. Check that the signer is the legitimate company (e.g. Adobe Systems) and that the signature is valid. A missing or invalid signature suggests the file was modified or forged (e.g. pirated software).
ex.az: 查看数码签署的签署者及是否有效。

cards.tz: 必须上网的应用：以加密防盗版
cards.en:
Enrichment: 'Internet connection required'. Why does a game or app need a constant Internet connection even if you are not playing online multiplayer?

When the game tries to connect to the Internet, it is actually processing data encryption and decryption. This technology aims to prevent illegal modification of the app such as cheating and pirated games.

Process (Fig 3.19):
  1. The user opens the game; it connects to the Internet.
  2. The server performs data encryption on important data/commands, e.g. in-game currency, HP, MP.
  3. The server sends the encrypted data to the device.
  4. The mobile device performs data decryption and runs the game.
Because key game data come from the server, a cracked offline copy cannot run, and players cannot easily edit their currency or HP locally. Cost to the user: no offline mode; some mobile data used.
cards.zh:
增润：“Internet connection required”。为何不玩联机游戏也要一直上网？

游戏连网时其实在进行数据加密及解密，目的是防止非法修改应用程式，例如作弊和盗版游戏。

流程（图 3.19）：
  1. 用户开启游戏并连网。
  2. 伺服器把重要数据/指令（如游戏货币、HP、MP）加密。
  3. 伺服器把加密数据传给装置。
  4. 手机解密后运行游戏。
由于关键数据来自伺服器，破解的离线版本无法运行，玩家也难以在本机修改货币或 HP。代价：没有离线模式，会用一些流动数据。

ex.q: A single-player mobile game shows 'No Connection – Try Again' when offline. Explain how this design protects the developer's IP.
ex.a: Key game data (in-game currency, HP, MP, commands) are encrypted on the developer's server and only decrypted on the device after connecting. Without the server, a pirated or modified copy cannot get valid data, which prevents pirated versions and cheating by modifying the app.
ex.az: 关键数据由伺服器加密后才下传，离线盗版及作弊难以运作。

mc.q: Which of the following actions may be seen as copyright infringement?
o: Downloading articles from an academic database.
Broadcasting a school event with permission.
Uploading films to the cloud storage and sharing them with friends.
Sending selfies to friends using peer-to-peer (P2P) software.
mc.e: Sharing copyrighted films without permission is unauthorised distribution (Internet piracy).
mc.ez: 未经许可分享电影属互联网盗版。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC1 (p.108)

mc.q: Janice takes the following actions on her work computer. Which of them is considered legal?
o: Sharing a commercial software with friends via the cloud.
Buying a CD and using the music in an event promotional video.
Using peer-to-peer (P2P) software to download a movie for personal use.
Sending freeware to colleagues via a BT program.
mc.e: Freeware may be copied and redistributed freely.
mc.ez: 免费软件可自由复制及分发。
mc.src: Textbook E Ch3 Chapter Exercise MC2 (p.108)

mc.q: Which may be considered copyright infringement? (1) Screenshot of a free online newspaper posted on social media (2) Using photos from an official website to sell a used product online (3) Photocopying one page of a 36-page recipe book for a school assignment (4) Removing the watermark from a copyrighted photo and uploading it to a personal website

User-locked: key locked to an account; any device while signed in.
